# ADR-018: The core is one work skill and one verifier, split by context and risk

**Status:** Accepted
**Date:** 2026-11-15
**Supersedes:** ADR-003 (agents split by cognitive mode) and ADR-007 (a persona id for every lifecycle plugin), and ADR-001 in part: its premise that the ecosystem is many role agents, each owning one stage. Its agent section structure, with its later amendments, stands.

## Decision

Work is decomposed by context and risk, not by lifecycle stage, role or cognitive mode.

- **Plugins:** `wisp` is the core; `courier`, `muse` and `mason` keep their ids; `wisp-packs` holds optional specializations. The lifecycle plugins are retired and what they knew becomes references loaded on demand.
- **One entry:** the `work` skill states a brief (outcome, constraints, evidence bar), sizes the change as contained, shared or irreversible, and picks a mode. `explore`, `spike`, `fix`, `build`, `check` and `ship` are one-line aliases into it.
- **One worker:** the primary agent researches, implements and tests in one context; forking a read-only search is a context split, not a role.
- **One independent check:** `wisp:verifier` gets the brief, the change and the evidence, never the worker's reasoning, runs things itself, and returns `verdict@3` under the round rules of ADR 013 and ADR 015. It runs for shared and irreversible work and for specs or plans that make claims about code.
- **Two helpers:** `adversary` settles one disputed finding; `recon` inventories an unfamiliar workspace.
- **No mandatory stages:** a spec or plan is written only for a shared contract or when the owner wants one. The owner sees a brief and decision cards in; the diff or render, evidence, a `Not verified:` list and the pull request out.
- **Must-hold rules are hooks:** a Stop hook asks once for the `Not verified:` list when changes are left uncommitted; the handback validator checks the verifier's `verdict@3`. Codex skills state both rules, because Codex has neither hook.

## Why

- **Agents are not a team of people:** role agents and handoff documents reproduced ceremony, and each handoff lost context.
- **Value sat in early independent checks:** first-round checks against code or a build produced the documented catches; later rounds, duplicate reviews and per-stage gates mostly added cost.
- **The pipeline mostly did not run:** work happened in general-purpose forks that rarely reached the skills, so their checks rarely ran. One entry is easier to reach.
- **Cost should follow risk:** the tier sets review depth, so contained work pays for executable evidence only.

## Rejected

- **Trim the pipeline and keep its stages:** because chained agents and mid-pipeline artifacts are the handoff pattern the evidence argues against, with the largest resident footprint.
- **One agent with hooks and tests only:** because it drops the independent first-round check that produced the catches; it survives as the contained tier.
- **One agent per cognitive mode:** because splitting evidence-gathering from judgment split context more than it protected judgment; the verifier does both in one fresh context.

## Consequences

- **Now true:** a handful of descriptions instead of dozens, and one place where independent verification lives; ADRs 011 to 016 still apply.
- **Cost:** consumers of the retired plugins lose those ids and skills; a long task can grow one context past what compaction preserves (fork a sub-task; do not add a role).
- **Risk:** the verifier's independence rests on fresh context and a checkable brief; a vague brief brings back padding and churn, so the verifier fails a brief with no evidence bar.
- **Revisit when:** paired fix-task sequences (`docs/evaluation-runbook.md`) show the verifier missing defects the retired spec or plan gates caught, a logic-bug class only a separate role caught, or a bare arm tying this design on hidden checks at lower cost above the contained tier.

## Evidence

- **Enforced by:** `tests/test_wisp_core.py` (agent set, tiers, description caps, aliases, hook behavior and registration) and `shared/hooks/validate-handback.py` (routes `wisp:verifier` to `verdict@3`).
- `docs/design/agent-native-architecture.md` (architecture B and the strategic layer); `docs/evaluations/frontend-design/IMPLEMENTATION-LOG.md`, "Evidence review and ADR 015".

183	## Capability Change Checklist
184	
185	For a change spanning Claude/AGY and Codex, read [`shared/harness-authoring.md`](./shared/harness-authoring.md) first. It defines which concerns are shared, which are native, and the counterpart-review record required before release.
186	
187	When you add or change what an existing agent can do — a new dimension, a new output status, a new default posture — the code change alone leaves the ecosystem inconsistent. Work through this list in the same change:
188	
189	- [ ] Frontmatter `description` reflects the new capability
190	- [ ] If the agent's output gained a new status/enum value, the plugin's `SKILL.md` names what the caller does with it — or states it's terminal
191	- [ ] New references live under the reader's concern, have a real caller, and update `shared/references/README.md` when they introduce a concern
192	- [ ] If runtime reference behavior changed, every consuming Claude/AGY and Codex route was reviewed and affected plugin versions were updated
193	- [ ] Every prose description still matches the agent's current behavior:
194	  - Plugin README subagent and output-schema sections
195	  - SKILL.md overview, dispatch, and I/O sections
196	  - Narrowed or corrected capabilities, not only additions
197	- [ ] Plugin `CHANGELOG.md` gets a new dated entry
198	- [ ] Version bumped in `plugin.json` only (see `shared/references/delivery/changesets.md`), then `just claude-manifests-sync && just marketplace-sync` write the README, marketplace, Claude and Codex copies; a bump needs no other hand edit
199	- [ ] `mason:scaffolder` and `mason:auditor` reflect any new structural convention; capability-only changes need no Mason update
200	
201	This isn't automated. `mason:audit-plugin` checks structural conformance; it does not (yet) check that every downstream doc/version file was updated to match a capability change. Until it does, this checklist is the thing standing between "the agent works" and "the ecosystem knows the agent works."
202	
203	---
204	
205	## Engineering Invariants
206	
207	- **No absolute paths:** prompt and skill paths are relative.
208	- **Self-contained subagents:** each prompt is readable in isolation and has no dependency on another agent's private prompt.
209	- **Pull, don't inject:** subagents load `shared/references/` on demand; the host does not preload them.
210	- **Authoring-only guidance:** never load `shared/agent-best-practices.md` at runtime.
211	- **Abstract tool language:** keep prompts portable across harnesses.
212	- **Conventional commits:** use the applicable type and plugin scope.
213	- **Clean writing:** omit AI filler, marketing language, and non-warning ALL CAPS.
214	- **Diagrams:** follow `shared/references/authoring/diagrams.md` when Mermaid materially clarifies a relationship.
215	
216	---
217	
218	## Releasing
219	
220	A release has three levels, and this marketplace installs from `main`:
221	
222	- **Shipped:** merged to `main` with the version bumped and the changelog entry written. Claude Code updates a plugin when its version changes, so this is what users get.
223	- **Pinned:** annotated git tags: `vX.Y.Z` for the ecosystem and `<plugin>--vA.B.C` for each plugin version, all on the merged commit. They give a rollback point and an exact version to install.
224	- **Announced:** a GitHub release for the ecosystem tag. Write its notes in `docs/releases/vX.Y.Z.md` (short highlights, then a pointer to the changelog); without that file the release uses the top changelog entry.
225	
226	After the version-bump PR merges, check out `origin/main` and run `just release --dry-run`, then `just release`. It checks the tree is clean and on `origin/main`, runs `just check`, creates and pushes the missing tags (your git configuration signs them) and creates the GitHub release. You run it, not an agent: it publishes.
227	
228	## Development Setup
229	
230	```bash
231	git clone https://github.com/orin-dx/wisp-plugins.git
232	cd wisp-plugins
233	
234	# Install pinned documentation-check dependencies (just and pnpm must be on PATH)
235	just install
236	
237	# Run every check
238	just check
239	```
240	
241	`just --list` shows each check as its own recipe (`just versions`, `just mermaid`, and so on) for running a subset while editing; a Mermaid syntax error is invisible to every other check — it's still valid markdown, `jq` never touches it, and it reads fine as source, so `just mermaid` is worth running on its own after touching a diagram. `just fmt` formats the repo in place with `oxfmt`; `just fmt-check` only verifies. Neither is part of `just check` yet — the repo doesn't have a baseline format pass, so `fmt-check` would fail on unrelated files today.
242	
243	Before a `git commit`, the repository-local Claude and Codex hook checks immutable schema versions and Codex generated-output freshness. See [`docs/repository-hooks.md`](./docs/repository-hooks.md).
244	
245	`just check` runs automatically in CI (`.github/workflows/validate.yml`) on every PR and every push to `main`.

- **Announced:** a GitHub release for the ecosystem tag. Write its notes in `docs/releases/vX.Y.Z.md` (short highlights, then a pointer to the changelog); without that file the release uses the top changelog entry.

After the version-bump PR merges, check out `origin/main` and run `just release --dry-run`, then `just release`. It checks the tree is clean and on `origin/main`, runs `just check`, creates and pushes the missing tags (your git configuration signs them) and creates the GitHub release. You run it, not an agent: it publishes.

## Development Setup

```bash
git clone https://github.com/orin-dx/wisp-plugins.git
cd wisp-plugins

# Install pinned documentation-check dependencies (just and pnpm must be on PATH)
just install

# Run every check
just check
```

`just --list` shows each check as its own recipe (`just versions`, `just mermaid`, and so on) for running a subset while editing; a Mermaid syntax error is invisible to every other check — it's still valid markdown, `jq` never touches it, and it reads fine as source, so `just mermaid` is worth running on its own after touching a diagram. `just fmt` formats the repo in place with `oxfmt`; `just fmt-check` only verifies. Neither is part of `just check` yet — the repo doesn't have a baseline format pass, so `fmt-check` would fail on unrelated files today.

Before a `git commit`, the repository-local Claude and Codex hook checks immutable schema versions and Codex generated-output freshness. See [`docs/repository-hooks.md`](./docs/repository-hooks.md).

`just check` runs automatically in CI (`.github/workflows/validate.yml`) on every PR and every push to `main`.

# Evaluation runbook

How to run the paired design in `docs/evaluation-methodology.md` on real work, for three task kinds. The question each time: does the treatment reduce turns and tokens, and does the first result need less rework? Single-run pilots and anecdotes cannot answer that. Pairs can, within the limits below.

`tools/transcript-metrics.py turns`, `agents`, `context` and `gates` measure; `tools/paired-analysis.py compare` and `agreement` analyse. `tests/test_transcript_metrics.py` (`DryRunTests`) runs this pipeline on synthetic sessions.

## Before any run

1. **Write the task list and the checklists first.** Take 6 to 10 real tasks from the backlog, each with a blinded checklist (see Scoring). Nothing is edited after the first run.
2. **Pin everything but the treatment.** Same model id, effort, repo commit, permission mode, and CLAUDE.md and memory. Record plugin versions and dates (methodology rule 10). Start each run in a fresh session from a clean checkout of the repo state.
3. **Randomize order.** Flip a coin per task for which arm runs first, so fatigue and your own learning do not fall on one arm. Run each pair on the same day.
4. **Run each arm per task once, then repeat** when you can: two to three runs, reduced to the median per task.
5. **One person drives, another scores.** The driver answers the agent's questions the same way in both arms (write the answers down on the first run and reuse them). Stop when the driver would accept the result; that is "acceptance".

## Capturing a session

The transcript is `~/.claude/projects/<encoded-project-dir>/<session-id>.jsonl` (read only; never copy it into the repo). For each finished run:

```
python3 tools/transcript-metrics.py turns --file <transcript> --trial task=T1,arm=control,run=1,score=0.7,defects=2 >> trials.jsonl
python3 tools/transcript-metrics.py context --match '<project-dir-suffix>$'
python3 tools/transcript-metrics.py agents --match '<project-dir-suffix>$'
python3 tools/transcript-metrics.py gates <directory holding <spec>-verdict[-n].json>
```

Add `gate_rounds=N` to `--trial` for the spec task and `ctx_chars=N` from `context`'s total. The `turns` fields: `prompts` (human prompts, the turns to acceptance), `turns` (assistant messages), `tool_calls`, `subagents`, `retries` (a call right after a failure, same tool, changed input; rework signal, defined in the tool docstring), `subagent_tokens` (as reported by subagents, not a bill). `context` is cumulative over the matched sessions, so match one session per run or use a dedicated project directory per arm.

Then:

```
python3 tools/paired-analysis.py compare trials.jsonl --baseline control --metrics score,prompts,turns,retries,subagent_tokens,gate_rounds
```

## Task kinds

### A. Design ideation (muse or sketch against an ad hoc session)

- **Statement**: "Explore <N=3> directions for <screen or component> in <repo>. Constraints: <list>. Stop when I can pick one."
- **Control**: plain session, no plugin, the same statement. **Treatment**: `muse:sketch` with the plugin installed.
- **Fixed**: model, effort, repo commit, design tokens and brief, the driver's selection rule (pick the option meeting the constraints; ties go to the first).
- **Primary metrics**: prompts to acceptance, `subagent_tokens`, `context` characters by origin, quality score, and whether the chosen direction survives promotion to a spec without being redone.
- **Defects found later**: constraint violations a reviewer finds in the accepted option within one week.

### B. Spec drafting and gating (gated pipeline now versus before gate hygiene)

- **Note**: the spec and gate plugins this kind compares were retired in v5 (ADR 018). Run it only from checkouts that still hold them, or adapt it to `wisp:verifier` checking a spec.
- **Statement**: "Draft and gate a spec for <requirement>" with a requirement of fixed text.
- **Control**: the plugins at commit `50bdcf1b^` (before the gate-hygiene change), checked out in a separate worktree and loaded as the plugin source. **Treatment**: the plugins at the commit under test. Disable the installed marketplace copy in both so only one version loads, and record the commit in each trial.
- **Fixed**: requirement text, model, effort, a prewritten set of answers to clarifying questions, retry cap.
- **Primary metrics**: `gate_rounds` (from `gates`), blockers per round, `subagent_tokens` from `agents`, prompts to a passed gate, long summaries and escalations.
- **Defects found later**: criteria that a reviewer who has not seen the gate verdicts finds untestable, missing an error case or contradicting the requirement; and spec contradictions raised when the spec is implemented.

### C. Changeset and PR text (courier with layered `changeset@3` guidance versus freehand)

- **Statement**: "Write the changeset and PR description for this diff" with a stored diff (`gh pr diff <n>` saved outside the repo, or a branch to check out).
- **Control**: freehand, no courier skills, no changeset guidance in context. **Treatment**: `courier:changeset` then `courier:pr`.
- **Fixed**: diff, repo conventions file and PR template, model, effort.
- **Primary metrics**: prompts to acceptance, `retries`, tokens (`agents` plus main-thread `context`), characters of text produced, quality score.
- **Defects found later**: a release reader's questions the text did not answer, wrong semver impact, missing limits or breaking-change marks, found by someone who did not write either text.

### D. Fix tasks in a sequence (`/wisp:fix` with and without the verifier)

- **Statement**: a series of 6 to 10 real fix tasks in one repository (for example findings from its review history), each stated as "fix this" with the claim to fix and the repository's own check command. Run them in order in one project, because savings from learned repository facts only show after about six tasks.
- **Control**: `/wisp:fix` with `wisp:verifier` withheld: one agent looping against the repository's CI-equivalent command, a test that fails on the original bug, and a search for the same mistake elsewhere. **Treatment**: the same, with `wisp:verifier` running (two rounds at most). A third arm with no plugin gives the bare baseline ADR 018 asks for. Pick tasks of shared-tier risk, so the verifier would run by default.
- **Fixed**: task order, repository commit per task, model, effort, the brief and evidence bar for each task.
- **Primary metrics**: prompts to acceptance, `retries`, tokens per task (`agents` plus main-thread `context`) and the trend across the sequence, verifier rounds.
- **Defects found later**: defects that escaped, found by a later review, CI, or a blind read by someone who did not write the fix. Score escapes per task, not just per sequence.

## Scoring

A scorer who did not run the sessions scores both outputs **blind**: strip arm names, plugin names and agent-specific markers, and shuffle. The checklist is written before the first run and frozen. Each item is yes, no or not applicable, with a one-line evidence note. Score = yes / (yes + no).

```
Task: ___  Output id (shuffled): ___  Scorer: ___  Date: ___
| # | Checklist item (observable, yes or no)        | Yes/No/NA | Evidence |
| 1 | <task-specific, written before the run>        |           |          |
Defects found in later review (count, with one line each): ___
Score: ___ / ___ = ___     Would accept as-is? yes / no
```

Calibration: for task kind B and C, have a second scorer (or an LLM judge) score at least 20 items, then run `python3 tools/paired-analysis.py agreement labels.json` with `[{"a": ..., "b": ...}]`. Use an LLM judge only at kappa of about 0.6 or above (convention, not measured). Below that, score by hand.

## How many pairs, and what a null shows

- The exact Wilcoxon test cannot reach p < 0.05 with fewer than 6 non-tied pairs, whatever the effect. Run **at least 6 pairs per task kind**; aim for 10, with repeats.
- With 6 to 10 pairs only large effects (on the order of a third of turns or tokens, or most items flipping in the checklist) can reach significance. A smaller real effect will look like noise.
- **A null result shows**: no large effect on that task kind, for that model and effort, on those tasks. **It does not show**: no effect, no effect at other efforts, or no effect on other repositories. Report the pair count, the median relative change with its direction, and the better, worse and tied counts. A consistent direction across tasks at n = 8 (say 7 of 8 better) is evidence worth following up, not proof.
- Do not mix kinds. Do not drop a task because the treatment lost. A crashed task is dropped from every arm and counted.
- Tag the write-up with `small-sample` and `self-benchmark` where they apply (`docs/evidence-quality.md`).

## Results table

```
| Task kind | Pairs | Prompts (median delta) | Turns | Retries | Subagent tokens | Gate rounds | Score (better/worse/tied) | Defects later | Verdict |
| A ideation |  |  |  |  |  | n/a |  |  |  |
| B spec gate |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| C changeset/PR |  |  |  |  | n/a |  |  |  |
| D fix sequence |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |
Provenance: model ___, effort ___, plugin commits ___ / ___, repo commit ___, dates ___, runs per task ___, excluded ___.
Power note and what would change the conclusion: ___
```

## Limits

Turn counts depend on how the driver answers. Subagent tokens are reported, not billed, and the main thread's tokens are not in them; `context` counts characters, not tokens, and ignores caching. Retries include legitimate progress. Treat the numbers as a comparison between arms on the same driver, not as absolute costs.

---
name: pr
description: >-
  Use this, not freehand text, whenever a pull request is opened or its title or description written or updated: "open a PR", "create a pull request", "write the PR description". Produces a PR title and body from the diff and any linked spec or requirement, then hands them to the branch's Entire trail, which opens the PR.
version: 2.0.2
---

# Courier — PR

<overview>
Produces a PR title and body from a diff plus optional linked spec/requirement, following the repository's pull request template when it has one, then opens the PR. Delegates the narrative to `pr-narrator`; opening the PR is a visible external action and always requires explicit confirmation before the `gh pr create` call fires.
</overview>

<dispatch>
| Agent | Model / Effort | Delegate When |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **pr-narrator** | sonnet / medium | A PR needs a title and body a reviewer with zero context can act on. |
</dispatch>

<references>
`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/shared/references/delivery/github.md` — outcome-led PR structure, observed verification, risk disclosure, review voice, labels, and `gh` commands.
</references>

<io>
**Consumes**: git diff, optionally linked `spec@1` or `requirement@1`
**Produces**: opened PR (title, body, labels). By default, push the branch and create or link its Entire trail (`entire trail create`); Entire opens the pull request from the trail, so return the title and body for it. Open a PR with `gh pr create` only when the repository's instructions say agents open them, and only after the user confirms the title and body.
</io>
---
name: changeset
description: >-
  Use this, not freehand text, whenever a changeset, changelog entry or release note is written or edited: "add a changeset", "write the changeset for PR 12", "update the changelog", "what should the release note say". Turns a diff into layered changeset@3 entries, one per user-visible outcome, or recommends none. Pass the criteria_evidence along when the work produced it.
version: 3.0.0
---

# Courier — Changeset

<overview>
A changeset is the changelog entry, written once at authoring time and later aggregated — not rewritten — into a release. `changeset-analyzer` decides what a consumer upgrading, scripting or setting up needs to know, works at the level of user-visible outcomes rather than pull requests, and writes each entry as a lead line plus bullets or audience sections when there is more to say. It can update an existing unreleased entry or recommend that none is needed. No length cap applies; detail follows what the reader needs. Delegates entirely to `changeset-analyzer`.
</overview>

<dispatch>
| Agent | Model / Effort | Delegate When |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **changeset-analyzer** | sonnet / medium | A git diff needs structured `changeset@3` entries, an update to an existing entry, or a recommendation that none is needed. |
</dispatch>

<references>
`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/shared/references/delivery/changesets.md` — changeset format, disposition, the Semver table (including CLI and serialized-file rows), entry shape, and the voice standard for this artifact.
</references>

<io>
**Consumes**: git diff (a single PR's, or a larger backlog/catch-up diff since the last release), optionally a linked `spec@1`, optionally the aggregated `criteria_evidence` the implementation produced
**Produces**: one or more `changeset@3` entries conforming to `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/shared/schemas/changeset@3.json` — one per user-visible outcome, never one entry bundling unrelated outcomes together. Route to `courier/pr` or `courier/release` depending on the next stage. When the repository keeps changesets as files (for example `.changeset/*.md`, written by `changeset add` or a project CLI such as `callisto add`), save each `new` or `update-existing` entry in that format with the package and the bump from `semver_impact`, using the repository's tool when it has one. A repository whose release PR aggregates changesets does not need `courier/release`.
</io>

A changeset is the changelog entry, written once at authoring time and later aggregated — not rewritten — into a release. `changeset-analyzer` decides what a consumer upgrading, scripting or setting up needs to know, works at the level of user-visible outcomes rather than pull requests, and writes each entry as a lead line plus bullets or audience sections when there is more to say. It can update an existing unreleased entry or recommend that none is needed. No length cap applies; detail follows what the reader needs. Delegates entirely to `changeset-analyzer`.
</overview>

<dispatch>
| Agent | Model / Effort | Delegate When |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **changeset-analyzer** | sonnet / medium | A git diff needs structured `changeset@3` entries, an update to an existing entry, or a recommendation that none is needed. |
</dispatch>

<references>
`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/shared/references/delivery/changesets.md` — changeset format, disposition, the Semver table (including CLI and serialized-file rows), entry shape, and the voice standard for this artifact.
</references>

<io>
**Consumes**: git diff (a single PR's, or a larger backlog/catch-up diff since the last release), optionally a linked `spec@1`, optionally the aggregated `criteria_evidence` the implementation produced
**Produces**: one or more `changeset@3` entries conforming to `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/shared/schemas/changeset@3.json` — one per user-visible outcome, never one entry bundling unrelated outcomes together. Route to `courier/pr` or `courier/release` depending on the next stage. When the repository keeps changesets as files (for example `.changeset/*.md`, written by `changeset add` or a project CLI such as `callisto add`), save each `new` or `update-existing` entry in that format with the package and the bump from `semver_impact`, using the repository's tool when it has one. A repository whose release PR aggregates changesets does not need `courier/release`.
</io>

Each rule ends with what enforces it: `[lint]` a lint or CI job, `[type]` the shape of the types, `[review]` nothing but review. Treat `[review]` rules as the likeliest to have drifted and check them in the area you touch. Run only the checks the repo declares (justfile, CI); say so when a check named here does not exist.

## Failure handling

- No `unwrap()` outside tests. `expect`, `panic!`, `unreachable!` and `todo!` follow the repo's lint table: where it denies them, use `?`; where it allows `expect`, the message names the invariant that makes the failure impossible. `[lint]` `unwrap_used` and friends in `[workspace.lints.clippy]`, run with `-D warnings`.
- `unsafe_code` is forbidden or denied workspace-wide, and `unused_must_use`, `let_underscore_must_use` and `map_err_ignore` are denied. A crate opts in with `[lints] workspace = true`. `[lint]`
- Failures are typed enums (`thiserror`; `miette::Diagnostic` for user-facing errors, with a stable code and a fix). No `String` variant when a structured one is possible; compose with `#[from]`/`#[source]`. Public error enums are `#[non_exhaustive]`. `[review]`
- Never degrade silently: a skipped file, dropped item or defaulted value emits a diagnostic or a count. When one sibling of a family starts failing loudly, convert the rest in the same change. About 20 of 406 review findings in these repos are silent degradation (an over-size file skipped with no count; one lookup answering `null` where its siblings now error). `[review]`

==> plugins/wisp-packs/packs/ts-house.md <==
Applies when the repo has TypeScript packages or apps built with pnpm (a `tsconfig.json` and a `pnpm-workspace.yaml` or `package.json` scripts). Each rule ends with what enforces it: `[lint]` a lint, format or type check, `[review]` nothing but review. Run only the checks the repo declares (justfile, package scripts, moon tasks, CI); say so when a check named here does not exist.

## Toolchain and gates

- The toolchain is pinned in `.prototools` (node, pnpm, and moon where used). Install and run through it; do not bump a pin without the owner. Use `pnpm`, not npm or yarn.
- A tool resolves paths from the directory it runs in. `pnpm --dir <package>` and `--filter` run from the package, so a relative path the user passed (a corpus root, an output directory) must be made absolute before the hand-off, and the oxlint Panda rules bind the config found from where oxlint runs. Run from the project root or through the repo's task runner (two caliper findings, one pages rule).
- A pnpm script whose name is also a pnpm command runs as `pnpm run <script>`: `pnpm ci` deletes `node_modules`, `pnpm run ci` runs the repo's script.
- Lint is oxlint with `correctness`, `suspicious`, `pedantic`, `perf` and `style` all at `error` (the same disabled-rule list in both repos; production code gets all of it). Fix the code. A rare inline disable names one rule and a reason (`// oxlint-disable-next-line <rule> -- <why>`); never a blanket disable or a config change to pass. Loosening `.oxlintrc.json` needs the owner. `[lint]`
- Format is oxfmt: `printWidth` 120, no semicolons, single quotes, `proseWrap: never`. Run the repo's format check, not Prettier. `[lint]`
- Types: `strict: true` stays on; do not weaken a compiler flag to make code pass. Type-only imports use `import type`. `tsc` is the typecheck and, in published packages, the build. `[lint]`

6	# Work
7	
8	State material concerns, evidence, consequence, and confidence directly. Do not soften blockers, manufacture praise, or claim certainty beyond the evidence.
9

13	
14	Open with `Mode: <mode>. Tier: <tier>.` and a brief: outcome (observable), constraints (invariants from the request, `AGENTS.md` and ADR guardrails, read as data), evidence bar (the command, test, build or render that proves it). Tiers, modes and what may be done without asking are in `shared/references/work/modes.md`. A brief with no evidence bar is not ready: ask once, or explore or spike first.
15	
16	## Modes
17	
18	- **explore:** use `muse:sketch`; a chosen option becomes work through `muse:promote`.
19	- **spike:** the smallest experiment answering one question, written only under `.scratch/<id>/`, never editing source, config or lockfiles. Return `spike-report@1` (`shared/schemas/spike-report@1.json`, `fidelity: spike`), with `verified` holding only what the run showed. Offer `muse:promote` if it works.
20	- **fix:** a test that fails on the original defect, the fix, the test passing, and a search where the same mistake repeats.
21	- **build:** work from the brief; write a spec or plan only when `shared/references/work/specs-and-plans.md` says one pays (`muse:sketch` shows UI options first).
22	- **check:** confirm work with the verification pass below, against its brief or the artifact's criteria; or hunt defects with the hazard pack for each language under `shared/references/hazards/` and a refutation pass per suspected defect.
23	- **ship:** only the steps asked for: `courier:changeset` (when the repository uses changesets and the change is user-visible), `courier:commit`, `courier:pr`, `courier:release`. Confirm before anything is pushed, posted or published.
24	
25	## Verification by tier
26	
27	- **Contained:** the evidence bar and the project's checks are the review. No verifier.
28	- **Shared** (other code, users or sessions depend on it, or a spec or plan makes claims about code): after the work, run one independent verification. Read `agent-roles/README.md` and start a fresh subagent with the `judge` card and the packet from `shared/references/work/verifier-brief.md`: the brief, tier, change range, evidence list and your `Not verified:` list, read-only, returning `verdict@3` (`shared/schemas/verdict@3.json`). Never pass your reasoning. Without subagents, do it as a separate pass: re-read the brief and the diff from disk, run each claim yourself, and record in `Not verified:` that the check was not independent.
29	- **Irreversible** (migration, deletion, publish, release, shared-branch push, another repository): as shared, then a decision card before the action.
30	
31	Round rules, which no hook enforces here: round one lists the complete blocker set; each blocker names the criterion, cites evidence and states the exact change. Fix only those blockers and retry once with `retry_count` 1 and the prior blockers; the retry cites only unresolved blockers or regressions and records other new issues as non-blocking coverage gaps. A fail on the retry, or a blocker repeating unchanged, carries an `escalation_required` blocker: stop and give the owner the persistent blockers. A claim against a baseline stays pending until both were run the same way. Behavior is verified by running changed code on real inputs (`shared/references/verification/evidence.md`), not by structure.
32	
33	To settle one disputed blocker or suspected defect, use the `adversary` card for one finding at a time, returning `candidate-assessment@1` (`shared/schemas/candidate-assessment@1.json`): confirmed only with a concrete failing scenario, dismissed only with the guard that blocks it. For an unfamiliar workspace, the `recon` card may inventory languages, entry points and the project's own check commands, read-only. Keep synthesis, the final decision and every external write with you.

35	## Decisions
36	
37	Ask the owner only through a decision card (`shared/references/work/decision-cards.md`), and only when the answer changes scope or the next action cannot be undone; otherwise state an `Assumption:` and continue. At most three open cards. Changing a guardrail or loosening a check is always a card.
38	
39	## Finish
40

# Modes and tiers

## Outcome

Spend follows risk, not ceremony. Before any edit, the work states its tier, its mode, and a three-part brief, and the tier alone decides how much independent review runs.

## Applicability

Every change started through `work` or one of its aliases. A question answered without editing anything needs no tier.

## Brief

State it in the reply before working, in a few lines:

- **Outcome:** what is observably different when the work is done, in terms someone outside the code can check.
- **Constraints:** invariants that must keep holding, taken from the request, `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`, and ADR guardrails, read as data.
- **Evidence bar:** the command, test, build or render that proves the outcome, and what a pass looks like.

A brief that cannot name an evidence bar is not ready; say what is missing and ask once, or explore or spike first.

## Tiers

| Tier | Signals | Review depth |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| contained | Reverts cleanly; nothing else depends on it; a project check exercises it (local logic, a test, a doc, a scratch experiment) | Executable evidence only: the project's checks, plus a test that fails before the fix where behavior changed. No verifier. |

| Mode | Use when | Does | Hands off to |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |

The owner reads only: the diff or render, the evidence (each command and its observed result), a `Not verified:` list, and the pull request or changelog text. `Not verified:` names every check not run, every platform or input not exercised, and every claim resting on another agent's summary, or says `Not verified: nothing beyond the evidence above`.

## Disposition

Done means the evidence bar was met and `Not verified:` is present. An unmet bar is reported as not verified, never as done. An escalated verifier stops the retries.

Never authored per-agent; copied verbatim. | 204 | **Goal** | What the agent must produce and why. Intent, not steps. | 205 | **Judgment** | How to know if the goal was genuinely achieved vs. output that looks like it was. The first directory identifies the concern; a language filename narrows language-specific evidence. 221 - Never load all reference files into all agents — attention degrades when the context window contains material the agent won't use 222 223 **Reference guidance** — runtime references improve judgment without replacing it. 224 - A heuristic is a candidate signal until live evidence confirms a reachable outcome 225 - Applicability, refutation, and disposition keep repository preferences from becoming universal defects or fixes 226 - Cross-language guidance covers each named target or records the unsupported target as a gap 227 228 **Radical candor** — agents state material concerns, evidence, consequence, and confidence directly. The tier alone sets review depth: contained work pays for the project's own checks and a failing-then-passing test; shared and irreversible work, and any spec or plan that makes claims about code, also goes to `wisp:verifier`. ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'flowchart': {'curve': 'basis', 'nodeSpacing': 40, 'rankSpacing': 56}, 'themeVariables': {'fontFamily': 'Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif', 'fontSize': '14px', 'lineColor': '#94a3b8', 'edgeLabelBackground': '#ffffff'}}}%% flowchart LR classDef source fill:#eef2ff,stroke:#6366f1,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#1e1b4b,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; classDef engine fill:#f5f3ff,stroke:#8b5cf6,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#4c1d95,rx:10px,ry:10px; classDef router fill:#fffbeb,stroke:#f59e0b,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#78350f,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; classDef output fill:#ecfdf5,stroke:#10b981,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#064e3b,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; classDef alert fill:#fff1f2,stroke:#f43f5e,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#881337,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; Brief["Brief
outcome, constraints, evidence bar"] --> Work{{"work
tier and mode"}} Work --> Do["Worker
one full context"] Do -->|"contained"| Out(["diff, evidence,
Not verified list"]) Do -->|"shared or irreversible"| Ver{{"wisp:verifier
opus · high · fresh context"}} Ver -->|"verdict@3 pass"| Out Ver -->|"fail: blockers only"| Do Do -.->|"round 2"| Ver Ver -.->|"fail again or repeated blocker"| Esc(["owner decides"]) class Brief source class Do engine class Work,Ver router class Out output class Esc alert ``` The verifier gets the brief, the change and the evidence, never the worker's reasoning, and runs code, a build or a render itself. It returns `verdict@3`: the complete blocker set in round one, and only known blockers or regressions on a retry (ADR 013). On `fail`, the worker receives **only the blockers array** and makes a targeted fix. The verifier gets two rounds: after the second fails, or when a blocker repeats, the circuit breaks and control passes to the owner (ADR 015). `retry_count` is tracked inside `verdict@3`; the caller sets it to the number of earlier rounds (0 in round one) and passes the prior blockers on a retry. A fail at `retry_count` 1 or later, or a repeated blocker, adds an `escalation_required` blocker. Three Claude Code hooks enforce what a prompt cannot, and all fail open: | Hook | Event | Registered by | Enforces | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `shared/hooks/validate-handback.py` | `PreToolUse` (`SubagentHandback`) | `wisp` | A `wisp:verifier` handback conforms to `verdict@3` and does not go past the two-round limit without escalating (ADR 012, 015); runs only in auto mode for local subagents | | `shared/hooks/stop-check.py` | `Stop` | `wisp` | With uncommitted changes, the final message carries a `Not verified:` line; it asks once (ADR 018) | | `shared/hooks/pack-inject.py` | `SessionStart` | `wisp-packs` | Injects the packs a repository names in a `Packs:` line of its `AGENTS.md` | A plugin registers a hook through `plugins//hooks/hooks.json`. The routing guard that redirected a direct agent call to its skill is gone: `wisp` has one entry point. Codex has none of these hooks and Antigravity's support is unverified; their skills state the same rules, and the agent loads a declared pack from the `AGENTS.md` line itself. --- ## 7. Agent Authoring Principles Full guide: `shared/agent-best-practices.md`. Key constraints: **4-part agent structure** — every Claude/AGY source agent defines: | Part | Purpose | | :--- | :--- | | **Constitution** | Ecosystem-wide invariants, byte-identical across every agent — the shared cache prefix. Never authored per-agent; copied verbatim. | | **Goal** | What the agent must produce and why. Intent, not steps. | | **Judgment** | How to know if the goal was genuinely achieved vs. output that looks like it was. Names the key failure mode. | | **Output** | Structured output shape, referencing a schema from `shared/schemas/` when the output flows to another agent. | No `` or `` body section (ADR 017); the frontmatter `role:` is a display label only. Codex skills and role cards use native structures. Cross-harness parity applies to route names, artifacts, evidence, and acceptance intent—not prompt sections or delegation topology. **Context and risk split** — work is divided by context and risk, not by role or cognitive mode (ADR 018). - One worker researches, implements and tests in one context; a second agent exists only for an independent check (`wisp:verifier`), one disputed finding (`wisp:adversary`), or a cheap read-only inventory (`wisp:recon`) - Agents are few: `wisp` has three, and adds no role agent, per-stage gate or mandatory spec or plan stage without a new ADR - Tiers: `haiku / low` for deterministic enumeration; `opus / high` for agents whose verdicts decide a finding (`wisp:verifier`, `wisp:adversary`); `sonnet / medium` for the rest (section 5) - Handoff documents between agents lose context, so independence rests on a fresh context and a checkable brief, not on more roles **Progressive context loading** — each agent loads only the focused references needed for its cognitive concern. - A `` block names each exact path it may load. The first directory identifies the concern; a language filename narrows language-specific evidence. - Never load all reference files into all agents — attention degrades when the context window contains material the agent won't use **Reference guidance** — runtime references improve judgment without replacing it. - A heuristic is a candidate signal until live evidence confirms a reachable outcome - Applicability, refutation, and disposition keep repository preferences from becoming universal defects or fixes - Cross-language guidance covers each named target or records the unsupported target as a gap **Radical candor** — agents state material concerns, evidence, consequence, and confidence directly. Friendly language stays respectful without softening blockers, manufacturing praise, or overstating certainty. **EARS for edges only** — EARS notation (`WHEN`, `IF`, `WHILE`, `WHERE`) belongs in output contracts and never-do rules. - Not in implementation steps or search strategies — those are the interior where agent judgment is the point - Over-constraining the interior caps the agent at the level of the author's imagination **Schema-driven handoffs** — where one agent's output is another's input, both reference the same schema file from `shared/schemas/`. The schema is the contract; the prompt describes the intent. --- ## 8. Cross-Harness Distribution The repository has one lifecycle contract and harness-specific execution packages. Claude Code and AGY consume the authored plugins directly; Codex consumes a generated, materialized marketplace. No custom server framework is required. ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'flowchart': {'curve': 'basis', 'nodeSpacing': 40, 'rankSpacing': 56}, 'themeVariables': {'fontFamily': 'Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif', 'fontSize': '14px', 'lineColor': '#94a3b8', 'edgeLabelBackground': '#ffffff'}}}%% flowchart LR classDef source fill:#eef2ff,stroke:#6366f1,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#1e1b4b,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; classDef store fill:#f8fafc,stroke:#64748b,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#0f172a,rx:10px,ry:10px; classDef engine fill:#f5f3ff,stroke:#8b5cf6,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#4c1d95,rx:10px,ry:10px; classDef output fill:#ecfdf5,stroke:#10b981,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#064e3b,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; ClaudeSource["Claude source

The schema is the cross-harness contract. Named agents, model routing, prompt wording, tool availability, and delegation strategy are harness-specific implementation details. - A source change is shared only when it affects plugin identity or a versioned artifact contract. - A workflow change is compatible only when both harnesses preserve the intended schema, evidence, and acceptance criteria; transcript or prose identity is not required. - Codex may use an agent team for independent work, but a missing team capability never blocks the single-agent workflow. Repository-local Entire adapters under `.agents/skills/`, `.claude/skills/`, `.cursor/`, `.gemini/skills/`, and `.opencode/` expose session-history search across supported hosts. They are Entire-managed development integrations, not Wisp plugin sources or Codex marketplace build inputs. --- ## 9. #!/usr/bin/env bash
# For each plugin, extracts every `plugin/skill-name` mention from a README
# table row (the "| `plugin/skill` | ... |" Skills table every split plugin
# uses) and checks a matching skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md exists. Scoped to
# table rows, not free prose, so a README that explicitly says "there is no
# `plugin/skill` to invoke" (the fix applied in v3.1.0) doesn't false-positive.
# Catches skills documented as real but never built or renamed without
# updating the docs — five plugins had this fixed in v3.1.0.
#
# Usage: scripts/check-skills-doc.sh

set -euo pipefail
script_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=lib/report.sh
source "$script_dir/lib/report.sh"
cd "$script_dir/.."

fail=0
count=0

for plugin_json in plugins/*/plugin.json; do
  dir="$(dirname "$plugin_json")"
  id="$(basename "$dir")"
  count=$((count + 1))

  mentions="$(grep -E "^\| \`${id}/[a-z0-9-]+\`" "$dir/README.md" 2>/dev/null \
              | grep -oE "\`${id}/[a-z0-9-]+\`" | tr -d '`' | sort -u || true)"

  missing=()
  while IFS= read -r mention; do
    [[ -z "$mention" ]] && continue
    skill="${mention#"${id}"/}"
    [[ -f "$dir/skills/$skill/SKILL.md" ]] || missing+=("$mention")
  done <<< "$mentions"

  if [[ ${#missing[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    fail=$((fail + 1))
    echo "FAIL: $id"
    for m in "${missing[@]}"; do
      echo "    documented but no skills/${m#"${id}"/}/SKILL.md: $m"
    done
  fi
done

report_check "$fail" "$count" \
  "plugin(s), every documented skill has a matching skills/ directory." \
  "plugin(s) document skills with no matching directory. Fix and re-run."

# Changelog

— muse

## [5.0.0] - 2026-11-15

### Removed
- The `component` skill and the `drafter`, `auditor` and `exit-gate` agents, with the plugin's hooks. Component specs and their gate belong to the work skill in the `wisp` plugin in v5; the UI-state and accessibility spec rules stay available as shared references.
- The `spec@1` and `verdict@3` outputs of this plugin. It no longer gates anything.

### Changed
- `muse` is now exploration and render only: `sketch` and `promote` with the `explorer` agent. `promote` hands the requirement to the `wisp` plugin instead of naming the retired spec and planning plugins.

## [1.2.0] - 2026-11-14

### Changed
- A direct call to one of this plugin's agents is redirected once per session to the skill that starts it, so that skill's checks run; a second call goes through (`shared/hooks/route-guard.py`, off with `WISP_ROUTE_GUARD=off`).
- The exit gate gets two rounds; after a second failing round, or a repeated blocker, the decision goes to you with the persistent blockers (ADR 015).
- The drafter self-checks and the gate judges; the auditor runs only when you ask, because it reviewed the same draft.
- The gate checks claims and citations against the code, build or spec they refer to; an issue it cannot tie to a source is a note.
- Unknowns no longer fail a component spec. The drafter states each in `scope` as an `Assumption:` or, when it changes scope, behavior other work depends on, or cost, an `Open decision:` that comes to you before the gate. The gate blocks only an unknown that leaves a criterion untestable or a decision you have not made (ADR 016).
- Pipeline agents' descriptions now say which skill starts them, so work goes through the skill where its checks run; they are also shorter.
- Agent prompts drop the `<backstory>` persona paragraph, leaving four sections; a paired ablation on three agents found no change in what they catch, in output size or in cost (ADR 017).

## [1.1.0] - 2026-11-10
# Changelog

— courier

## [5.0.0] - 2026-11-15

### Removed
- The `release-summarizer` and `review-preprocessor` agents. Both did deterministic work: aggregating changesets by their own `semver_impact`, and bundling a diff, spec, test results and open questions. `courier/release` and `courier/receive-feedback` now do that themselves in the primary agent and return the same `release-artifact@3` and review package. `commit-analyzer`, `pr-narrator` and `changeset-analyzer` stay.

### Changed
- `courier/changeset` takes the `criteria_evidence` an implementation produced from whatever source, no longer from `smith` only, since `smith` is retired in v5.
- `courier/post-review` no longer names `sentinel` as an owner of spec-conformance review.

## [3.2.0] - 2026-11-14

### Changed
- Changesets follow the owner's changelog convention: a bold lead-in naming the change as the user sees it, its value, then short bullets for why, how to adopt and limits, with bold labels instead of headings; breaking changes and required steps go in their own `**Breaking:**` and `**Action:**` paragraphs so release tools list them.
- `courier:pr` hands the title and body to the branch's Entire trail by default; Entire opens the PR. It opens one itself only where a repository says agents do.
- Changesets follow the repository's own rules and file format (`.changeset/*.md`, its CLI and contributing guide) and are saved there with the package and bump, instead of only returned as JSON.
- `courier:pr` does not open a pull request when the repository says another system (for example Entire) opens them.
# Changelog

— wisp

## [1.0.0] - 2026-11-15

### Added
- One `work` skill that sizes a change as contained, shared or irreversible, states its outcome, constraints and evidence bar before any edit, and picks the mode and review depth. You are asked only for decisions that change scope or cannot be undone, as decision cards.

# Agent-native architecture: design it twice

**Status: option B was implemented as v5 in PR 24 on 2026-11-16 and recorded in [ADR 018](../adr/018-deep-core-by-context-and-risk.md), which superseded ADR 003 and 007 and part of 001.** The sections below are the proposal as written, kept as the reasoning; they are not updated. Deferred or still open:

- **Measurement (section 5):** no arm has been run against another. The fix-task kind now exists as kind D in [`docs/evaluation-runbook.md`](../evaluation-runbook.md); the paired run, the pre-registered thresholds and the replay are not done, so B's advantage over A and C is unproven.
- **The UI pack:** a design or UI pack for `wisp-packs` is not built; only the Rust and TypeScript house packs ship.
- **The strategic layer (section 3):** detectors, the monitor step and the unattended loop are not built. Only the Stop hook and decision cards from the no-regret list shipped.
- **Antigravity:** whether the v5 plugins, hooks and pack injection work there is not verified.
- **Open questions (section 6):** answers are not recorded here.

The question: the plugins mirror a human organization (role-named agents, handoff documents, sign-off gates). Agents are not a team of people, and models trained on human organizations reproduce that ceremony unless asked not to. What shape should the architecture take instead, and how do we find out?

Method: each option below is chosen by a different **unit of decomposition**, because the options must differ in structure, not in parameters. A splits by lifecycle stage and role. B splits by context and risk. C splits by what a machine can check.

## 1. Goal and constraints

**Goal for the owner.** Set direction once, and read only what matters: a brief and decision cards in; a diff or render, the evidence, a list of what was not verified, and the changelog or PR out. Spend scales with risk, not with ceremony. Must-hold rules are enforced, not requested.

**Goal for agents.** Work from outcome, constraints and an evidence bar rather than a procedure. Hold the full context of one change. Be checked by something a machine can run. Get independent review only where a confident mistake is costly or irreversible.

Constraints used in the comparison (C1 to C10):

- **C1, owner attention:** artifacts reach the owner only at the edges and at decisions that change direction.
- **C2, cost follows risk:** tokens, rounds and review depth scale with reversibility and blast radius.
- **C3, independent check where it pays:** fresh-context verification where a confident mistake is costly or irreversible.
- **C4, must-hold rules are deterministic:** hooks, tests, types and lints, not prompts.
- **C5, reached by default:** the right path runs without the model having to choose a skill.
- **C6, full context for the worker:** pieces that must be read together are joined (Ousterhout), without becoming one mega-agent.
- **C7, strategy is asked for:** the architecture contains the explicit step that asks "what should be structurally different", because models do not volunteer it.
- **C8, resident footprint:** always-loaded descriptions and plugins are a cost.
- **C9, migration cost and reversibility:** what existing records, schemas, tests and Codex counterparts must change.
- **C10, portability:** Claude Code and Antigravity share the authored tree, Codex has its own; hooks exist on each host but differ ([ARCHITECTURE.md](../../ARCHITECTURE.md) section 8).

**Evidence base shared by all three, and its limits.** One author, five projects, September to November 2026, single runs for nearly every pilot. Records: [Evidence review and ADR 015](../evaluations/frontend-design/IMPLEMENTATION-LOG.md#evidence-review-and-adr-015), [ADR evidence](../evaluations/frontend-design/IMPLEMENTATION-LOG.md#adr-evidence), [the architecture review](../evaluations/frontend-design/ARCHITECTURE-REVIEW.md), [the assumptions register](../architecture-assumptions.md) (rows 2, 7, 8, 9, 14 are the ones this touches).

- **Value came from first-round independent checks against code or a build.** Repeated rounds, duplicate review of one draft, per-commit review and mutation on logic-free code were waste. The catch-rate counts are approximate in part (reconstructed from an agent's notes).
- **"No reviewer caught a logic bug" is an absence in a sample, not a proof.** Humans found logic bugs (28% of human-found findings), so the gap is real, but the sample cannot say reviewers could never catch them.
- **77% of subagent tokens went to ad hoc forks and general-purpose agents.** Those are reported tokens, not a bill, and forks are not all waste; the figure says where work happened, not that it was wasteful.
- **Plugin agents mostly ran without their skills** (7 skill calls in 812 transcripts), so the checks inside skills mostly did not run ([unused agents](../evaluations/frontend-design/investigations/unused-agents.md)).
- **The cost figures from TokenEconomizer** (pruning unused tools was the largest saving; failed trajectories take about a third of spend) are the owner's citation. They were not re-read for this document and carry the `vendor-run` and `testimonial` cautions of [evidence quality](../evidence-quality.md) until they are.
- **No arm has been run against another.** Nothing here is a comparison of A, B and C; section 5 is how to get one.

## 2. Three structurally different architectures

### A. Today's plugins, trimmed

**Shape.** The lifecycle pipeline as it stands after [ADR 015](../adr/015-two-rounds-one-reality-check.md) and the routing guard: 11 plugins, 44 agents, 39 skills (counted in `plugins/` now). `guide` offers six intent commands that hand off to the existing skills. Further trimming that stays inside A: collapse the build-side chain (recon, implementer, mutator, reviewer, exit gate), make plugins opt-in per project instead of always loaded, delete agents the sessions never reached, and keep typed artifacts as handoffs.

**Who does what.** The model routes (through `guide`, the project's `AGENTS.md`, or typing a command). A skill orchestrates role-and-mode agents. Gates are default-fail with two rounds. A hook validates gate output and redirects direct agent calls to the skill ([ADR 012](../adr/012-gate-output-enforced-by-hook.md), [ARCHITECTURE.md](../../ARCHITECTURE.md) section 6).

**What humans see.** Requirement, research report, spec, plan, verdicts, review artifacts: written documents mid-pipeline, plus the final PR text.

**How checks work.** Independent gates on artifacts (spec, plan, implementation), default to fail, schema-checked, capped at two rounds; mutation and review per batch.

**What it removes.** Round 3 and beyond, the default auditor step, per-commit review, mutation on logic-free code, a prompt-only retry cap.

**Cost and risk.**

- Still the largest resident surface: agent and skill descriptions, 33 skills a person must pick between.
- Routing still depends on the model: the guard acts only on a direct agent call; a generic "review my fix" was handled with no skill or agent at all (log, "Routing: entry commands and the routing guard").

---
name: sketch
description: Explore several structurally different options for a design or approach, rendered and shown before they are described, with a decision log. Use this, rather than describing options in prose, when the user wants to see options before deciding what to build. Non-binding: no gate, no spec, no tests.
---

State material concerns, evidence, consequence, and confidence directly. Do not soften blockers, manufacture praise, or claim certainty beyond the evidence.

# Show options before deciding

Open with "Mode: sketch. Nothing here is binding." This is the light path: there is no gate, no spec and no test requirement, open questions are allowed, and the work stops before implementing. If the request is a shared component, something other code depends on, or behavior and accessibility that must not regress, say the work skill in the `wisp` plugin fits better (it specifies and checks the contract) and let the user choose. Read `shared/references/architecture/modes.md` for the mode rules.

## Inputs

- Free-text intent, an existing `option-set@1` to continue, or a `requirement@1` for context.
- The project's brand, stack, tokens and real content, when they exist.

## Workflow

1. Write the anchor brief: the problem, the audience, the constraints and the non-goals. Ask at most three short questions, and only when an answer would change the options; otherwise state assumptions and continue.
2. For design work, in the first round propose four distinct, concrete directions, one line each, and let the user pick one. If they say "you choose", pick and say why. Later rounds stay inside the chosen direction.
3. Name three structural bets (five at most) that differ in arrangement, interaction model or information hierarchy, not in color or spacing. Replace any option that differs only in tint.
4. Build each option as a minimal static page (HTML and CSS, no build step) under `.scratch/<id>/<option-id>/`, using real content and tokens. Mark placeholder text as placeholder; invent no numbers, claims or testimonials.
5. Render each option at the viewports and themes in the brief (default 390x844 and 1440x900, light and dark when the project has both) with the project's Playwright script, a browser tool, or the sandboxed browser if the host provides one. Write `.scratch/<id>/board.html` listing each option's title, status, summary and renders side by side. Make each preview frame tall enough to show the whole option (at least 640px) and let the board scroll; a clipped preview hides the design. Present the renders before explaining them. If nothing can render, say so and give the one command that opens the files; never describe a render you did not see. Keep command output and scripts out of the thread as `shared/references/tooling/context.md` says. Look at one render at a time.
6. Record the decision. Set each option's `status` to `chosen`, `rejected` or `parked` with a `reason`, and append a dated entry to `decisions`. Never rewrite an earlier entry or reuse an option id. For another round, re-read the brief and restate it in a line; after about four rounds, restate it and start from it, because options drift.
7. Write the `option-set@1` (conforming to `shared/schemas/option-set@1.json`, with `fidelity` set to `sketch`) to `docs/sketches/<id>.json`, list the assumptions and open questions, and stop. Offer another round, `promote`, or dropping it, and end with one line: "Skipped by design: spec, tests and gates."

## Record shape

```json
{
{
  "name": "wisp",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "description": "Start any change by sizing its risk, stating outcome, constraints and evidence bar, and verifying shared or irreversible work with fresh eyes.",
  "author": {
    "name": "Gabriel Castro",
    "email": "gabe@techworx.dev"
  },
  "homepage": "https://github.com/orin-dx/wisp-plugins",
  "repository": "https://github.com/orin-dx/wisp-plugins",
  "license": "MIT",
  "keywords": [
    "workflow",
    "verification",
    "risk",
    "fix",
    "build"
  ],
  "skills": "./skills/",
  "interface": {
    "displayName": "Wisp",
    "shortDescription": "Size the change, prove it, verify where it pays",
    "longDescription": "One work skill that classifies a change as contained, shared or irreversible, states its brief before editing, picks the mode, and spends independent verification only on shared or irreversible work.",
    "developerName": "Gabriel Castro (Orin DX)",
    "category": "Developer Tools",
    "capabilities": [
      "Interactive",
      "Read",
      "Write"
    ],
    "websiteURL": "https://github.com/orin-dx/wisp-plugins",
    "defaultPrompt": [
      "Fix this bug with a test that fails first",
      "Is this change done? Verify it",
      "Spike whether this library works here"
    ]
  }
}

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Measure plugin and agent use from Claude Code session transcripts and persisted gate verdicts.

Subcommands (all read-only, standard library only):

  agents   Subagent calls, reported tokens and minutes per agent type per session, with the share
           spent by plugin agents (types containing ":") against everything else, and flags for
           tasks whose reported tokens pass --cliff (default 200000). Tokens are what each subagent
           reported, not a bill; the flag approximates the long-context pricing tier and cannot see
           per-request context size.
  skills   Skill and slash-command invocations against agent invocations per session. A plugin
           whose skills are never invoked never runs the agents that only its skills start.
  gates    Rounds per spec, final verdict, blockers per round, retry counts above 3, summaries over
           300 characters and escalations, from verdict files named <spec>-verdict[-<n>].json.
  outputs  Share of tool-result characters by tool, and the ceiling a compressor that only sees one
           tool (default Bash) could reach: share of that tool times the assumed reduction.

  context  Where characters entering the conversation come from, per category: user text,
           assistant text, tool calls (agent delegation prompts counted apart), tool results by tool
           (agent results are the handoffs), plus the single largest results. Characters, not
           tokens: divide by about 4 for a rough token count. Use it to decide what to keep out of
           context before cutting anything.

  turns    Per session: human prompts, assistant turns, tool calls, subagent spawns, retries and
           subagent tokens, for "turns to acceptance" and "rework" in a paired evaluation. Select
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Paired analysis of an evaluation with two or more arms, using only the standard library.

Input is a JSON list (or JSON Lines) of trials:
  {"task": "t1", "arm": "baseline", "run": 1, "score": 0.5, "cost": 0.21, "turns": 14, "error": false}
Any numeric field other than task and run can be compared; "score" is treated as the quality
outcome. Rules, taken from the paired benchmarks this repository learned from:

  * Pair by task. Repeated runs of a task in one arm are reduced to their median.
  * A task that has no successful trial in some arm is excluded from every arm, so one crash cannot
    skew a comparison. The number excluded is reported.
  * Compare each other arm with the baseline on every metric: median of the per-task differences,
    the median relative change, an exact two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank p-value (normal approximation
    above 60 pairs), and for the quality score an exact two-sided sign test on the non-ties with the
    counts of better, worse and tied tasks.
  * Report the power limit: a small number of pairs can only rule out large effects.

A tool's self-reported saving is a claim about its counterfactual, not about your bill; analyse the
measured cost and the graded outcome, never the tool's own scoreboard.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Snapshot Entire review findings for one or more repositories and summarize them.

Subcommands (standard library only; `pull` needs the `entire` CLI, logged in, with network access):

  pull     Write every finding (open, resolved, dismissed) on every change of the given repositories to a JSON file.
  summary  Print counts per repository by status and severity, changes with findings, and findings per change,
           for one snapshot or for two snapshots side by side (before and after).

Examples:
  python3 tools/entire-findings.py pull --project gh/orin-dx --repos caliper callisto monokl --out findings-2026-11-06.json
  python3 tools/entire-findings.py summary findings-2026-11-06.json
  python3 tools/entire-findings.py summary before.json after.json
"""

# Decision cards

## Outcome

The owner decides only what changes scope or cannot be undone, in under a minute per decision, and the answer survives the session.

## Applicability

Raise a card when the answer changes scope, behavior other work depends on, or cost the owner carries, or when the next action is irreversible (`shared/references/work/modes.md`, Tiers and Autonomy). Everything else proceeds on a stated assumption: write `Assumption: <the answer the work proceeds on>` in the reply and keep going.

No trigger, no card. A preference question, a naming choice, or a step the repository already answers is not a card.

## Shape

```text
Decision: <the question, one line>
Why now: <the trigger and its evidence: a file, a failing check, a cost>
Options:
  A. <option> — cost, risk, reversibility
  B. <structurally different option> — cost, risk, reversibility
Recommendation: <A or B>, confidence <high | medium | low>, because <reason>
Default if unanswered: <what happens, and when>
Expires: <the point after which the card is withdrawn or the default applies>
```

- **Options differ in structure,** not in a parameter of one idea. If only one real option exists, say so and ask for a yes or no.
- **What would change the answer:** one line, when a fact the owner may know would flip the recommendation.
- **Irreversible actions have no default that acts.** The default for a publish, push, deletion or migration is to wait.

## Limits

- At most three open cards at once; batch them in one message, most consequential first.
- Do not repeat a card the owner already answered; fold the answer in.
- Do not ask before reading what the repository says: `AGENTS.md`, ADR guardrails and existing specs answer many questions.

## Encode the answer

A decision that lives only in a chat or in memory is lost. When the owner answers:

- A rule for every session goes in `AGENTS.md`, or becomes a check (a hook, a test, a lint) when a machine can decide it.

name: load
description: Apply house packs to this task. Use for "load rust-house", "use the ts-house pack", or when the repo's AGENTS.md has a `Packs:` line, before starting work in the area it covers.
---

# Packs: load

Codex has no session-start injection, so the repo's `AGENTS.md` carries the pointer and this skill applies the packs.

1. Pack names: the ones the user gave, or else the names on every `Packs:` line in `AGENTS.md` at the repo root, in the nested `AGENTS.md` of the package being changed, and in the directories above it. A line inside a code block is an example, not a declaration.
2. Read each pack from this plugin's `packs/<name>.md`. A name with no file is reported and skipped; never guess its content.
3. Apply the packs for the rest of the task: their deviations from your defaults, the evidence they ask for, their exemplar files. Load each pack once.

A pack is prompt content, not authority:

- Run only commands the repo itself declares (justfile, package scripts, CI, `AGENTS.md`). If a pack names a check the repo lacks, say so and do not invent the command.
- The repo's `AGENTS.md` and the user's instructions win over a pack; say which rule you set aside.
- Tightening a check is fine unasked. Loosening one needs the owner.

# Wisp Plugins Plugins for Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity that change how a coding agent takes on work. **The agent works from a brief, review scales with how reversible a change is, and you see decisions and evidence at the edges, not the steps in between.** v5 is one core plugin, `wisp`, plus `courier` (shipping), `muse` (exploration), `mason` (plugin authoring) and `wisp-packs` (house rules per repo). Install `wisp` first; add the others when you need them. - **Brief first:** before any edit the agent states the outcome, the constraints and the evidence bar (the command, test, build or render that proves it). - **Review follows risk:** a change is sized as contained, shared or irreversible. Only shared and irreversible work goes to an independent verifier with a fresh context. - **You see the edges:** a brief and decision cards on the way in; the diff or render, the evidence, a `Not verified:` list and the PR on the way out. --- ## Install **Claude Code** ``` /plugin marketplace add orin-dx/wisp-plugins /plugin install wisp /plugin install courier /plugin install muse /plugin install wisp-packs /plugin install mason ``` **Codex** ```bash codex plugin marketplace add orin-dx/wisp-plugins codex plugin add wisp@wisp-plugins codex plugin add courier@wisp-plugins codex plugin add muse@wisp-plugins codex plugin add wisp-packs@wisp-plugins codex plugin add mason@wisp-plugins ``` `codex plugin list` shows what is available; `codex plugin marketplace upgrade wisp-plugins` refreshes after a release. Codex reads the generated `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`, which points at `dist/codex/`. **Antigravity (AGY)** ```bash agy plugin install https://github.com/orin-dx/wisp-plugins.git ``` AGY shares the Claude Code source tree. Whether the v5 hooks and pack injection work there is not verified. The community [`agy-plugins-cli`](https://github.com/ZaunEkko/agy-plugins-cli) (`agy-plugin marketplace add orin-dx/wisp-plugins`, then `agy-plugin add @wisp-plugins`) may not find plugins under `plugins/`; that install path is also not verified. **Set it up for a project.** To have everyone on a repo get the plugins, commit this to `.claude/settings.json`: ```json { "extraKnownMarketplaces": { "wisp-plugins": { "source": { "source": "github", "repo": "orin-dx/wisp-plugins" } } }, "enabledPlugins": { "wisp@wisp-plugins": true, "courier@wisp-plugins": true, "wisp-packs@wisp-plugins": true } } ``` and add this to the repo's `AGENTS.md` (the `Packs:` line is optional; see [Packs](#packs)): ```markdown ## Work Start changes with /wisp:work (or /wisp:fix, /wisp:build, /wisp:check, /wisp:spike, /wisp:explore, /wisp:ship). State the tier, the brief and the evidence bar first; end with the evidence and a "Not verified:" list. Each hook fails open: if it breaks, the session carries on. | Hook | Plugin, event | Does | Switch | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `shared/hooks/stop-check.py` | `wisp`, Stop | When the work tree has uncommitted changes and the final message has no `Not verified:` line, asks once for one | `WISP_STOP_CHECK=off` turns it off | | `shared/hooks/validate-handback.py` | `wisp`, PreToolUse `SubagentHandback` | Rejects a `wisp:verifier` report that is not a valid `verdict@3`, or that goes past the second round without escalating. Runs in auto mode for local subagents only. | `WISP_HANDBACK_TRACE=` logs each inspected event; `WISP_HANDBACK_STATE_DIR` sets where denial counts are kept (default: `wisp-handback` in the temp directory) | | `shared/hooks/pack-inject.py` | `wisp-packs`, SessionStart | Injects the packs named on `Packs:` lines in `AGENTS.md` | Remove the `Packs:` line, or disable `wisp-packs` | On Codex the `wisp` skills state the `Not verified:` and round rules themselves, and packs load through `load`. --- ## Packs A pack is a short markdown file on how one owner builds in one area: when it applies, where the house rules differ from a model's defaults, the checks that enforce them, and a file to imitate. Packs come from real repos and review findings. | Pack | Applies when | | :--- | :--- | | `rust-house` | The repo is a Rust workspace (a `Cargo.toml` with `[workspace]`) | | `ts-house` | The repo has TypeScript packages or apps built with pnpm | **Adopt one:** add `Packs: rust-house` (several: `Packs: rust-house, ts-house`) to the `AGENTS.md` where it applies. In a monorepo, put it in the package's nested `AGENTS.md`. The hook reads `AGENTS.md` from the working directory up to the repo root and up to four levels below. Unknown names and lines inside code blocks are ignored. **Try one:** `/wisp-packs:load rust-house` for this session only. `/wisp-packs:list` shows available and declared packs; `/wisp-packs:suggest` recommends packs for the repo and edits nothing. **Rules a pack follows:** it never adds a command the repo does not declare; the repo's `AGENTS.md` and your instructions win over it; it may tighten a check but loosening one needs the owner. **Write one:** add `plugins/wisp-packs/packs/.md` (lowercase letters, digits and hyphens). The first line says when it applies. Each rule states the outcome and ends with what enforces it: `[lint]`, `[type]` or `[review]`. End with an exemplar file. A rule goes in a shared pack only when it holds in at least two repos. Then run `just marketplace-sync` so the Codex bundle carries it. See [`plugins/wisp-packs/`](./plugins/wisp-packs/). --- ## Shipping `/wisp:ship` runs only the steps you ask for, in this order, and confirms before anything leaves the machine: 1. **Changeset** (`courier:changeset`), when the repo uses changesets and the change is user-visible: one `changeset@3` entry per user-visible outcome, or a recommendation that none is needed. A repo that keeps `.changeset/*.md` files gets them in its own format and tool. 2. **Commit** (`courier:commit`): a conventional commit message that explains why. 3. **Pull request** (`courier:pr`): a title and body for a reviewer with no context. By default it pushes the branch and creates or links the branch's Entire trail (`entire trail create`), and Entire opens the PR. It runs `gh pr create` only when the repo's instructions say agents open PRs, and only after you confirm. 4. **Release notes** (`courier:release`): aggregates changesets since the last release into a `release-artifact@3`. It runs `just check`, creates and pushes the missing tags, and publishes the GitHub release (`--notes FILE` picks the notes, `--yes` skips the prompt). A person runs it, not an agent. Details: [CONTRIBUTING.md, Releasing](./CONTRIBUTING.md#releasing). --- ## Harness differences | | Claude Code | Codex | Antigravity | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | Source | `plugins//` | Separately written skills in `harnesses/codex/plugins//`, built into `dist/codex/` | `plugins//`, shared with Claude Code | | Verifier | Named agent `wisp:verifier` (opus/high) | A fresh subagent with the `judge` role card; without subagents, a separate pass recorded in `Not verified:` as not independent | Not verified | | Stop hook, handback hook | Yes | No; the skills state both rules | Not verified | | Packs | Injected at session start | `load` reads the `Packs:` line and applies the packs | Not verified; use `load` | | Model tiers | Honoured from agent frontmatter | Host-selected | AGY applies its own routing | Artifacts are the same versioned JSON schemas in `shared/schemas/` on every harness. Background: [ARCHITECTURE.md section 8](./ARCHITECTURE.md#8-cross-harness-distribution). --- ## Migrating from v4 v5 replaces the eight pipeline plugins with `wisp`. Their schemas stay in `shared/schemas/`, unchanged, so existing artifacts still validate. | v4 plugin | What to use in v5 | | :--- | :--- | | `weaver` (capture and prioritize requirements) | `/wisp:work` with the need in plain words; `muse:promote` writes a `requirement@1` from a chosen sketch or spike | | `vanguard` (research) | `/wisp:work` or `/wisp:spike`: the worker researches in its own context | | `scribe` (specs) | `/wisp:build`, which writes a spec only where one pays; the verifier checks specs that make claims about code | | `navigator` (plans) | `/wisp:build`, which writes a plan only where one pays | | `smith` (implement, spike) | `/wisp:build`, `/wisp:fix`, `/wisp:spike` | | `sentinel` (gates) | `/wisp:check` (the verifier) | | `ranger` (bug hunts) | `/wisp:check` asked to find bugs: hazard references plus the adversary per suspected bug | | `guide` (intent commands) | The same six commands under `wisp`: `/wisp:explore`, `spike`, `fix`, `build`, `check`, `ship` | | `muse` component specs (`component` skill, drafter, auditor, exit gate) | `/wisp:build`; `muse` keeps only `sketch` and `promote` | | `courier` release-summarizer and review-preprocessor agents | Nothing to do: `courier:release` and `courier:receive-feedback` do that work themselves, with the same outputs | **Breaking changes and what to do:** - **The eight plugin ids are gone.** Install `wisp` and remove `weaver`, `vanguard`, `scribe`, `navigator`, `smith`, `sentinel`, `ranger` and `guide` from your settings (`enabledPlugins` in `.claude/settings.json`, or your harness's plugin list). - **No mandatory spec, plan or sign-off stage.** If a project's `AGENTS.md` tells agents to run the old skills, replace that with the [Work snippet](#install). - **`muse` no longer gates anything** and no longer produces `spec@1` or `verdict@3`. - **The routing guard and `WISP_ROUTE_GUARD` are gone**; `wisp` has one entry point. Full list: [CHANGELOG.md](./CHANGELOG.md). --- ## Evaluate and tune Whether v5 beats the old pipeline or a bare agent is not yet measured.
