input.content:
# Wisp Plugins Plugins for Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity that change how a coding agent takes on work. **The agent works from a brief, review scales with how reversible a change is, and you see decisions and evidence at the edges, not the steps in between.** v5 is one core plugin, `wisp`, plus `courier` (shipping), `muse` (exploration), `wisp-packs` (house rules per repo) and `mason` (plugin authoring). Install `wisp` first; add the others when you need them. - **Brief first:** before any edit the agent states the outcome, the constraints and the evidence bar (the command, test, build or render that proves it). - **Review follows risk:** each change is sized as contained, shared or irreversible. Only shared and irreversible work goes to an independent verifier with a fresh context. - **You see the edges:** a brief and decision cards on the way in; the diff or render, the evidence, a `Not verified:` list and the PR on the way out. --- ## Install **Claude Code** ``` /plugin marketplace add orin-dx/wisp-plugins /plugin install wisp /plugin install courier /plugin install muse /plugin install wisp-packs /plugin install mason ``` **Codex** ```bash codex plugin marketplace add orin-dx/wisp-plugins codex plugin add wisp@wisp-plugins codex plugin add courier@wisp-plugins codex plugin add muse@wisp-plugins codex plugin add wisp-packs@wisp-plugins codex plugin add mason@wisp-plugins ``` `codex plugin list` shows what is available; `codex plugin marketplace upgrade wisp-plugins` refreshes after a release. Codex reads the generated `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`, which points at `dist/codex/`. From a local checkout: `python3 tools/build-codex-marketplace.py`, then `codex plugin marketplace add .`. **Antigravity (AGY)** ```bash agy plugin install https://github.com/orin-dx/wisp-plugins.git ``` AGY uses the same source tree as Claude Code. Whether the v5 hooks and pack injection work there is not verified. The community [`agy-plugins-cli`](https://github.com/ZaunEkko/agy-plugins-cli) (`agy-plugin marketplace add orin-dx/wisp-plugins`, then `agy-plugin add @wisp-plugins`) may not find plugins under `plugins/`; that path is not verified either. **Set it up for a project.** So everyone on a repo gets the plugins in Claude Code, commit this to `.claude/settings.json`: ```json { "extraKnownMarketplaces": { "wisp-plugins": { "source": { "source": "github", "repo": "orin-dx/wisp-plugins" } } }, "enabledPlugins": { "wisp@wisp-plugins": true, "courier@wisp-plugins": true, "wisp-packs@wisp-plugins": true } } ``` and add this to the repo's `AGENTS.md`, which every harness reads (the `Packs:` line is optional; see [Packs](#packs)): ```markdown ## Work Start changes with /wisp:work (or /wisp:fix, /wisp:build, /wisp:check, /wisp:spike, /wisp:explore, /wisp:ship). State the tier, the brief and the evidence bar first; end with the evidence and a "Not verified:" list. Packs: rust-house ``` **Registered the old marketplace id?** Run `/plugin marketplace remove orin-dx-agent-plugins` (Claude Code) or `codex plugin marketplace remove orin-dx-agent-plugins` (Codex), then add `orin-dx/wisp-plugins` as above. Upgrading from v4: see [Migrating from v4](#migrating-from-v4). --- ## Quick start Start with `/wisp:work` and describe the change; it picks the mode. Or start a mode directly: | Command | Use it when | Example | What comes back | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `/wisp:work` | Any change, or you are not sure which mode fits | `/wisp:work the export drops rows with empty dates` | The mode it chose, then as below | | `/wisp:explore` | You want to see options before deciding | `/wisp:explore three layouts for the settings page` | Rendered options and a decision log (`option-set@1`) through `muse:sketch` | | `/wisp:spike` | You want to know whether something works here | `/wisp:spike does this queue library run on our Node version?` | A `spike-report@1`: what ran, what was verified, what was not; files only under `.scratch//` | | `/wisp:fix` | Something is broken, or a review left findings | `/wisp:fix login fails when the email has a plus sign` | A test that failed before and passes after, the fix, and other places with the same mistake | | `/wisp:build` | You are building something real | `/wisp:build add CSV import to the contacts API` | The change and its evidence; a spec or plan only where one pays | | `/wisp:check` | You want work verified, or bugs found | `/wisp:check is the retry change done?` | A `verdict@3` from the verifier, or suspected bugs each confirmed or dismissed | | `/wisp:ship` | The work is ready to go out | `/wisp:ship changeset and PR` | Only the courier steps you asked for, confirmed before anything is pushed, posted or published | Every reply opens with the mode, the tier and the brief, and ends with the evidence and what was not checked. An abridged, made-up example: ```text Mode: fix. Tier: shared. Outcome: a login with "a+b@x.com" succeeds. Constraints: the session token format does not change (AGENTS.md). Evidence bar: the repo's test command passes, with a new test that fails on the old code. ...work... Evidence: test command: the new test failed before the fix; all tests pass after. Verifier: pass, round 1. Not verified: the mobile client; SSO logins were not exercised. Next: /wisp:ship ``` When a decision changes scope or cannot be undone, you get a **decision card**: the question, two or three structurally different options, a recommendation, and what happens if you do not answer. Everything else proceeds on a stated `Assumption:`. --- ## The plugin set | Plugin | Use it for | Commands | Agents (tier) | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | [`wisp`](./plugins/wisp/) | Every change: sizes it, states the brief, does the work, verifies where it pays | `work`, `explore`, `spike`, `fix`, `build`, `check`, `ship` | `verifier`, `adversary` (opus/high); `recon` (haiku/low) | | [`courier`](./plugins/courier/) | Commit messages, PRs, changesets, review feedback, release notes | `commit`, `pr`, `changeset`, `receive-feedback`, `post-review`, `release` | `pr-narrator`, `changeset-analyzer` (sonnet/medium); `commit-analyzer` (haiku/low) | | [`muse`](./plugins/muse/) | Seeing rendered options before deciding, and turning the chosen one into work | `sketch`, `promote` | `explorer` (sonnet/medium) | | [`wisp-packs`](./plugins/wisp-packs/) | Making the agent build the way your other repos are built | `load`, `list`, `suggest` | none | | [`mason`](./plugins/mason/) | Building, auditing and evaluating plugins like these | `scaffold-plugin`, `audit-plugin`, `design-schema`, `scaffold-subagent`, `evaluate` | `auditor`, `scaffolder`, `schema-designer` (sonnet/medium); `evaluation-runner` (haiku/low); `evaluation-adjudicator` (opus/high) | In Claude Code a command is `/:`, for example `/courier:pr` or `/wisp-packs:load rust-house`. --- ## How it works ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'flowchart': {'curve': 'basis', 'nodeSpacing': 40, 'rankSpacing': 56}, 'themeVariables': {'fontFamily': 'Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif', 'fontSize': '14px', 'lineColor': '#94a3b8', 'edgeLabelBackground': '#ffffff'}}}%% flowchart LR classDef source fill:#eef2ff,stroke:#6366f1,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#1e1b4b,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; # Wisp Plugins Plugins for Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity that change how a coding agent takes on work. **The agent works from a brief, review scales with how reversible a change is, and you see decisions and evidence at the edges, not the steps in between.** v5 is one core plugin, `wisp`, plus `courier` (shipping), `muse` (exploration), `wisp-packs` (house rules per repo) and `mason` (plugin authoring). Install `wisp` first; add the others when you need them. - **Brief first:** before any edit the agent states the outcome, the constraints and the evidence bar (the command, test, build or render that proves it). - **Review follows risk:** each change is sized as contained, shared or irreversible. Only shared and irreversible work goes to an independent verifier with a fresh context. - **You see the edges:** a brief and decision cards on the way in; the diff or render, the evidence, a `Not verified:` list and the PR on the way out. --- ## Install **Claude Code** ``` /plugin marketplace add orin-dx/wisp-plugins /plugin install wisp /plugin install courier /plugin install muse /plugin install wisp-packs /plugin install mason ``` **Codex** ```bash codex plugin marketplace add orin-dx/wisp-plugins codex plugin add wisp@wisp-plugins codex plugin add courier@wisp-plugins codex plugin add muse@wisp-plugins codex plugin add wisp-packs@wisp-plugins codex plugin add mason@wisp-plugins ``` `codex plugin list` shows what is available; `codex plugin marketplace upgrade wisp-plugins` refreshes after a release. Codex reads the generated `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`, which points at `dist/codex/`. From a local checkout: `python3 tools/build-codex-marketplace.py`, then `codex plugin marketplace add .`. **Antigravity (AGY)** ```bash agy plugin install https://github.com/orin-dx/wisp-plugins.git ``` AGY uses the same source tree as Claude Code. Whether the v5 hooks and pack injection work there is not verified. The community [`agy-plugins-cli`](https://github.com/ZaunEkko/agy-plugins-cli) (`agy-plugin marketplace add orin-dx/wisp-plugins`, then `agy-plugin add @wisp-plugins`) may not find plugins under `plugins/`; that path is not verified either. **Set it up for a project.** So everyone on a repo gets the plugins in Claude Code, commit this to `.claude/settings.json`: ```json { "extraKnownMarketplaces": { "wisp-plugins": { "source": { "source": "github", "repo": "orin-dx/wisp-plugins" } } }, "enabledPlugins": { "wisp@wisp-plugins": true, "courier@wisp-plugins": true, "wisp-packs@wisp-plugins": true } } ``` and add this to the repo's `AGENTS.md`, which every harness reads (the `Packs:` line is optional; see [Packs](#packs)): ```markdown ## Work Start changes with /wisp:work (or /wisp:fix, /wisp:build, /wisp:check, /wisp:spike, /wisp:explore, /wisp:ship). State the tier, the brief and the evidence bar first; end with the evidence and a "Not verified:" list. Packs: rust-house ``` **Registered the old marketplace id?** Run `/plugin marketplace remove orin-dx-agent-plugins` (Claude Code) or `codex plugin marketplace remove orin-dx-agent-plugins` (Codex), then add `orin-dx/wisp-plugins` as above. Upgrading from v4: see [Migrating from v4](#migrating-from-v4). --- ## Quick start Start with `/wisp:work` and describe the change; it picks the mode. Or start a mode directly: | Command | Use it when | Example | What comes back | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `/wisp:work` | Any change, or you are not sure which mode fits | `/wisp:work the export drops rows with empty dates` | The mode it chose, then as below | | `/wisp:explore` | You want to see options before deciding | `/wisp:explore three layouts for the settings page` | Rendered options and a decision log (`option-set@1`) through `muse:sketch` | | `/wisp:spike` | You want to know whether something works here | `/wisp:spike does this queue library run on our Node version?` | A `spike-report@1`: what ran, what was verified, what was not; files only under `.scratch//` | | `/wisp:fix` | Something is broken, or a review left findings | `/wisp:fix login fails when the email has a plus sign` | A test that failed before and passes after, the fix, and other places with the same mistake | | `/wisp:build` | You are building something real | `/wisp:build add CSV import to the contacts API` | The change and its evidence; a spec or plan only where one pays | | `/wisp:check` | You want work verified, or bugs found | `/wisp:check is the retry change done?` | A `verdict@3` from the verifier, or suspected bugs each confirmed or dismissed | | `/wisp:ship` | The work is ready to go out | `/wisp:ship changeset and PR` | Only the courier steps you asked for, confirmed before anything is pushed, posted or published | Every reply opens with the mode, the tier and the brief, and ends with the evidence and what was not checked. An abridged, made-up example: ```text Mode: fix. Tier: shared. Outcome: a login with "a+b@x.com" succeeds. Constraints: the session token format does not change (AGENTS.md). Evidence bar: the repo's test command passes, with a new test that fails on the old code. ...work... Evidence: test command: the new test failed before the fix; all tests pass after. Verifier: pass, round 1. Not verified: the mobile client; SSO logins were not exercised. # Wisp Plugins Plugins for Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity that change how a coding agent takes on work, and the agent-side companions to the [Wisp](https://github.com/orin-dx/wisp) project-intelligence library. **The agent works from a brief, review scales with how reversible a change is, and you see decisions and evidence at the edges, not the steps in between.** v5 is one core plugin, `wisp`, plus `courier` (shipping), `muse` (exploration), `wisp-packs` (house rules per repo) and `mason` (plugin authoring). Install `wisp` first; add the others when you need them. - **Brief first:** before any edit the agent states the outcome, the constraints and the evidence bar (the command, test, build or render that proves it). - **Review follows risk:** each change is sized as contained, shared or irreversible. Only shared and irreversible work goes to an independent verifier with a fresh context. - **You see the edges:** a brief and decision cards on the way in; the diff or render, the evidence, a `Not verified:` list and the PR on the way out. --- ## Install **Claude Code** ``` /plugin marketplace add orin-dx/wisp-plugins /plugin install wisp /plugin install courier /plugin install muse /plugin install wisp-packs /plugin install mason ``` **Codex** ```bash codex plugin marketplace add orin-dx/wisp-plugins codex plugin add wisp@wisp-plugins codex plugin add courier@wisp-plugins codex plugin add muse@wisp-plugins codex plugin add wisp-packs@wisp-plugins codex plugin add mason@wisp-plugins ``` `codex plugin list` shows what is available; `codex plugin marketplace upgrade wisp-plugins` refreshes after a release. Codex reads the generated `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`, which points at `dist/codex/`. From a local checkout: `python3 tools/build-codex-marketplace.py`, then `codex plugin marketplace add .`. **Antigravity (AGY)** ```bash agy plugin install https://github.com/orin-dx/wisp-plugins.git ``` AGY uses the same source tree as Claude Code. Whether the v5 hooks and pack injection work there is not verified. The community [`agy-plugins-cli`](https://github.com/ZaunEkko/agy-plugins-cli) (`agy-plugin marketplace add orin-dx/wisp-plugins`, then `agy-plugin add @wisp-plugins`) may not find plugins under `plugins/`; that path is not verified either. **Set it up for a project.** So everyone on a repo gets the plugins in Claude Code, commit this to `.claude/settings.json`: ```json { "extraKnownMarketplaces": { "wisp-plugins": { "source": { "source": "github", "repo": "orin-dx/wisp-plugins" } } }, "enabledPlugins": { "wisp@wisp-plugins": true, "courier@wisp-plugins": true, "wisp-packs@wisp-plugins": true } } ``` and add this to the repo's `AGENTS.md`, which every harness reads (the `Packs:` line is optional; see [Packs](#packs)): ```markdown ## Work Start changes with /wisp:work (or /wisp:fix, /wisp:build, /wisp:check, /wisp:spike, /wisp:explore, /wisp:ship). State the tier, the brief and the evidence bar first; end with the evidence and a "Not verified:" list. Packs: rust-house ``` **Registered the old marketplace id?** Run `/plugin marketplace remove orin-dx-agent-plugins` (Claude Code) or `codex plugin marketplace remove orin-dx-agent-plugins` (Codex), then add `orin-dx/wisp-plugins` as above. Upgrading from v4: see [Migrating from v4](#migrating-from-v4). --- ## Quick start Start with `/wisp:work` and describe the change; it picks the mode. Or start a mode directly: | Command | Use it when | Example | What comes back | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `/wisp:work` | Any change, or you are not sure which mode fits | `/wisp:work the export drops rows with empty dates` | The mode it chose, then as below | | `/wisp:explore` | You want to see options before deciding | `/wisp:explore three layouts for the settings page` | Rendered options and a decision log (`option-set@1`) through `muse:sketch` | | `/wisp:spike` | You want to know whether something works here | `/wisp:spike does this queue library run on our Node version?` | A `spike-report@1`: what ran, what was verified, what was not; files only under `.scratch//` | | `/wisp:fix` | Something is broken, or a review left findings | `/wisp:fix login fails when the email has a plus sign` | A test that failed before and passes after, the fix, and other places with the same mistake | | `/wisp:build` | You are building something real | `/wisp:build add CSV import to the contacts API` | The change and its evidence; a spec or plan only where one pays | | `/wisp:check` | You want work verified, or bugs found | `/wisp:check is the retry change done?` | A `verdict@3` from the verifier, or suspected bugs each confirmed or dismissed | | `/wisp:ship` | The work is ready to go out | `/wisp:ship changeset and PR` | Only the courier steps you asked for, confirmed before anything is pushed, posted or published | Every reply opens with the mode, the tier and the brief, and ends with the evidence and what was not checked. An abridged, made-up example: ```text Mode: fix. Tier: shared. Outcome: a login with "a+b@x.com" succeeds. Constraints: the session token format does not change (AGENTS.md). Evidence bar: the repo's test command passes, with a new test that fails on the old code. ...work... Evidence: test command: the new test failed before the fix; all tests pass after. Verifier: pass, round 1. Not verified: the mobile client; SSO logins were not exercised. # Wisp Plugins Plugins for Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity that change how a coding agent takes on work, and the agent-side companions to the [Wisp](https://github.com/orin-dx/wisp) project-intelligence library. **The agent works from a brief, review scales with how reversible a change is, and you see decisions and evidence at the edges, not the steps in between.** v5 is one core plugin, `wisp`, plus `courier` (shipping), `muse` (exploration), `wisp-packs` (house rules per repo) and `mason` (plugin authoring). Install `wisp` first; add the others when you need them. - **Brief first:** before any edit the agent states the outcome, the constraints and the evidence bar (the command, test, build or render that proves it). - **Review follows risk:** each change is sized as contained, shared or irreversible. Only shared and irreversible work goes to an independent verifier with a fresh context. - **You see the edges:** a brief and decision cards on the way in; the diff or render, the evidence, a `Not verified:` list and the PR on the way out. --- ## Install **Claude Code** ``` /plugin marketplace add orin-dx/wisp-plugins /plugin install wisp /plugin install courier /plugin install muse /plugin install wisp-packs /plugin install mason ``` **Codex** ```bash codex plugin marketplace add orin-dx/wisp-plugins codex plugin add wisp@wisp-plugins codex plugin add courier@wisp-plugins codex plugin add muse@wisp-plugins codex plugin add wisp-packs@wisp-plugins codex plugin add mason@wisp-plugins ``` `codex plugin list` shows what is available; `codex plugin marketplace upgrade wisp-plugins` refreshes after a release. Codex reads the generated `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`, which points at `dist/codex/`. From a local checkout: `python3 tools/build-codex-marketplace.py`, then `codex plugin marketplace add .`. **Antigravity (AGY)** ```bash agy plugin install https://github.com/orin-dx/wisp-plugins.git ``` AGY uses the same source tree as Claude Code. Whether the v5 hooks and pack injection work there is not verified. The community [`agy-plugins-cli`](https://github.com/ZaunEkko/agy-plugins-cli) (`agy-plugin marketplace add orin-dx/wisp-plugins`, then `agy-plugin add @wisp-plugins`) may not find plugins under `plugins/`; that path is not verified either. **Set it up for a project.** So everyone on a repo gets the plugins in Claude Code, commit this to `.claude/settings.json`: ```json { "extraKnownMarketplaces": { "wisp-plugins": { "source": { "source": "github", "repo": "orin-dx/wisp-plugins" } } }, "enabledPlugins": { "wisp@wisp-plugins": true, "courier@wisp-plugins": true, "wisp-packs@wisp-plugins": true } } ``` and add this to the repo's `AGENTS.md`, which every harness reads (the `Packs:` line is optional; see [Packs](#packs)): ```markdown ## Work Start changes with /wisp:work (or /wisp:fix, /wisp:build, /wisp:check, /wisp:spike, /wisp:explore, /wisp:ship). State the tier, the brief and the evidence bar first; end with the evidence and a "Not verified:" list. Packs: rust-house ``` **Registered the old marketplace id?** Run `/plugin marketplace remove orin-dx-agent-plugins` (Claude Code) or `codex plugin marketplace remove orin-dx-agent-plugins` (Codex), then add `orin-dx/wisp-plugins` as above. Upgrading from v4: see [Migrating from v4](#migrating-from-v4). --- ## Quick start Start with `/wisp:work` and describe the change; it picks the mode. Or start a mode directly: | Command | Use it when | Example | What comes back | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `/wisp:work` | Any change, or you are not sure which mode fits | `/wisp:work the export drops rows with empty dates` | The mode it chose, then as below | | `/wisp:explore` | You want to see options before deciding | `/wisp:explore three layouts for the settings page` | Rendered options and a decision log (`option-set@1`) through `muse:sketch` | | `/wisp:spike` | You want to know whether something works here | `/wisp:spike does this queue library run on our Node version?` | A `spike-report@1`: what ran, what was verified, what was not; files only under `.scratch//` | | `/wisp:fix` | Something is broken, or a review left findings | `/wisp:fix login fails when the email has a plus sign` | A test that failed before and passes after, the fix, and other places with the same mistake | | `/wisp:build` | You are building something real | `/wisp:build add CSV import to the contacts API` | The change and its evidence; a spec or plan only where one pays | | `/wisp:check` | You want work verified, or bugs found | `/wisp:check is the retry change done?` | A `verdict@3` from the verifier, or suspected bugs each confirmed or dismissed | | `/wisp:ship` | The work is ready to go out | `/wisp:ship changeset and PR` | Only the courier steps you asked for, confirmed before anything is pushed, posted or published | Every reply opens with the mode, the tier and the brief, and ends with the evidence and what was not checked. An abridged, made-up example: ```text Mode: fix. Tier: shared. Outcome: a login with "a+b@x.com" succeeds. Constraints: the session token format does not change (AGENTS.md). Evidence bar: the repo's test command passes, with a new test that fails on the old code. ...work... Evidence: test command: the new test failed before the fix; all tests pass after. Verifier: pass, round 1. Not verified: the mobile client; SSO logins were not exercised. Next: /wisp:ship ``` When a decision changes scope or cannot be undone, you get a **decision card**: the question, two or three structurally different options, a recommendation, and what happens if you do not answer. Everything else proceeds on a stated `Assumption:`. --- ## The plugin set | Plugin | Use it for | Commands | Agents (tier) | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | [`wisp`](./plugins/wisp/) | Every change: sizes it, states the brief, does the work, verifies where it pays | `work`, `explore`, `spike`, `fix`, `build`, `check`, `ship` | `verifier`, `adversary` (opus/high); `recon` (haiku/low) | | [`courier`](./plugins/courier/) | Commit messages, PRs, changesets, review feedback, release notes | `commit`, `pr`, `changeset`, `receive-feedback`, `post-review`, `release` | `pr-narrator`, `changeset-analyzer` (sonnet/medium); `commit-analyzer` (haiku/low) | | [`muse`](./plugins/muse/) | Seeing rendered options before deciding, and turning the chosen one into work | `sketch`, `promote` | `explorer` (sonnet/medium) | | [`wisp-packs`](./plugins/wisp-packs/) | Making the agent build the way your other repos are built | `load`, `list`, `suggest` | none | | [`mason`](./plugins/mason/) | Building, auditing and evaluating plugins like these | `scaffold-plugin`, `audit-plugin`, `design-schema`, `scaffold-subagent`, `evaluate` | `auditor`, `scaffolder`, `schema-designer` (sonnet/medium); `evaluation-runner` (haiku/low); `evaluation-adjudicator` (opus/high) | In Claude Code a command is `/:`, for example `/courier:pr` or `/wisp-packs:load rust-house`. --- ## How it works ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'flowchart': {'curve': 'basis', 'nodeSpacing': 40, 'rankSpacing': 56}, 'themeVariables': {'fontFamily': 'Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif', 'fontSize': '14px', 'lineColor': '#94a3b8', 'edgeLabelBackground': '#ffffff'}}}%% flowchart LR classDef source fill:#eef2ff,stroke:#6366f1,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#1e1b4b,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; /wisp:work or a mode"] --> Work{{"work

researches, edits, tests

persistent blockers"]) Out -->|"irreversible: decision card first"| Ship["courier

No verifier. | | shared | Other code, users or sessions depend on it, or a spec or plan makes claims about code | The same, then the verifier: one round and one targeted retry, then the persistent blockers come to you | | irreversible | Hard to undo, or crosses the repo boundary: migration, deletion, publish, release, push to a shared branch | The verifier, then a decision card before the action itself | When two tiers fit, the higher one applies. The verifier gets the brief, the change and the evidence, never the worker's reasoning, and runs the code, build or render itself. Details: [`shared/references/work/modes.md`](./shared/references/work/modes.md) and [ADR 018](./docs/adr/018-deep-core-by-context-and-risk.md). --- ## Hooks and switches These run in Claude Code only. Each fails open: if a hook breaks, the session carries on. | Hook | Plugin, event | Does | Switch | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `shared/hooks/stop-check.py` | `wisp`, Stop | When the work tree has uncommitted changes and the final message has no `Not verified:` line, asks once for one | `WISP_STOP_CHECK=off` turns it off | | `shared/hooks/validate-handback.py` | `wisp`, PreToolUse `SubagentHandback` | Rejects a `wisp:verifier` report that is not a valid `verdict@3`, or that goes past the second round without escalating. Runs in auto mode, for local subagents only. | `WISP_HANDBACK_TRACE=` logs each inspected event; `WISP_HANDBACK_STATE_DIR` sets where denial counts are kept (default `wisp-handback` in the temp directory) | | `shared/hooks/pack-inject.py` | `wisp-packs`, SessionStart | Injects the packs named on `Packs:` lines in `AGENTS.md` | Remove the `Packs:` line, or disable `wisp-packs` | On Codex the `wisp` skills state the `Not verified:` and round rules themselves, and packs load through `load`. --- ## Packs A pack is a short markdown file on how one owner builds in one area: when it applies, where the house rules differ from what a model would do by default, the checks that enforce them, and a file to imitate. Packs are mined from real repos and review findings. | Pack | Applies when | | :--- | :--- | | `rust-house` | The repo is a Rust workspace (a `Cargo.toml` with `[workspace]`) | | `ts-house` | The repo has TypeScript packages or apps built with pnpm | - **Adopt one:** add `Packs: rust-house` (several: `Packs: rust-house, ts-house`) to the `AGENTS.md` where it applies; in a monorepo, the package's nested `AGENTS.md`. The hook reads `AGENTS.md` from the working directory up to the repo root and up to four levels below. Unknown names and lines inside code blocks are ignored. - **Try one:** `/wisp-packs:load rust-house` applies it for this session. `/wisp-packs:list` shows available and declared packs; `/wisp-packs:suggest` recommends packs for the repo and edits nothing. - **What a pack may do:** it never adds a command the repo does not declare; the repo's `AGENTS.md` and your instructions win over it; it may tighten a check, but loosening one needs the owner. - **Write one:** add `plugins/wisp-packs/packs/.md` (lowercase letters, digits and hyphens). The first line says when it applies. Each rule states the outcome and ends with what enforces it: `[lint]`, `[type]` or `[review]`. End with a file to imitate. A rule goes in a shared pack only when it holds in at least two repos. Run `just marketplace-sync` so the Codex bundle carries it. More: [`plugins/wisp-packs/`](./plugins/wisp-packs/). --- ## Shipping `/wisp:ship` runs only the steps you ask for, in this order, and confirms with you before anything leaves the machine: 1. **Changeset** (`courier:changeset`), when the repo uses changesets and the change is user-visible: one `changeset@3` entry per user-visible outcome, or a recommendation that none is needed. By default it pushes the branch and creates or links the branch's Entire trail (`entire trail create`), and Entire opens the PR. It runs `gh pr create` only when the repo's instructions say agents open PRs, and only after you confirm. 4. **Release notes** (`courier:release`): aggregates changesets since the last release into a `release-artifact@3`. # Wisp Plugins Plugins for Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity that change how a coding agent takes on work, and the agent-side companions to the [Wisp](https://github.com/orin-dx/wisp) project-intelligence library. **The agent works from a brief, review scales with how reversible a change is, and you see decisions and evidence at the edges, not the steps in between.** v5 is one core plugin, `wisp`, plus `courier` (shipping), `muse` (exploration), `wisp-packs` (house rules per repo) and `mason` (plugin authoring). Install `wisp` first; add the others when you need them. - **Brief first:** before any edit the agent states the outcome, the constraints and the evidence bar (the command, test, build or render that proves it). - **Review follows risk:** each change is sized as contained, shared or irreversible. Only shared and irreversible work goes to an independent verifier with a fresh context. - **You see the edges:** a brief and decision cards on the way in; the diff or render, the evidence, a `Not verified:` list and the PR on the way out. --- ## Install **Claude Code** ``` /plugin marketplace add orin-dx/wisp-plugins /plugin install wisp /plugin install courier /plugin install muse /plugin install wisp-packs /plugin install mason ``` **Codex** ```bash codex plugin marketplace add orin-dx/wisp-plugins codex plugin add wisp@wisp-plugins codex plugin add courier@wisp-plugins codex plugin add muse@wisp-plugins codex plugin add wisp-packs@wisp-plugins codex plugin add mason@wisp-plugins ``` `codex plugin list` shows what is available; `codex plugin marketplace upgrade wisp-plugins` refreshes after a release. Codex reads the generated `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`, which points at `dist/codex/`. From a local checkout: `python3 tools/build-codex-marketplace.py`, then `codex plugin marketplace add .`. **Antigravity (AGY)** ```bash agy plugin install https://github.com/orin-dx/wisp-plugins.git ``` AGY uses the same source tree as Claude Code. Whether the v5 hooks and pack injection work there is not verified. The community [`agy-plugins-cli`](https://github.com/ZaunEkko/agy-plugins-cli) (`agy-plugin marketplace add orin-dx/wisp-plugins`, then `agy-plugin add @wisp-plugins`) may not find plugins under `plugins/`; that path is not verified either. **Set it up for a project.** So everyone on a repo gets the plugins in Claude Code, commit this to `.claude/settings.json`: ```json { "extraKnownMarketplaces": { "wisp-plugins": { "source": { "source": "github", "repo": "orin-dx/wisp-plugins" } } }, "enabledPlugins": { "wisp@wisp-plugins": true, "courier@wisp-plugins": true, "wisp-packs@wisp-plugins": true } } ``` and add this to the repo's `AGENTS.md`, which every harness reads (the `Packs:` line is optional; see [Packs](#packs)): ```markdown ## Work Start changes with /wisp:work (or /wisp:fix, /wisp:build, /wisp:check, /wisp:spike, /wisp:explore, /wisp:ship). State the tier, the brief and the evidence bar first; end with the evidence and a "Not verified:" list. Packs: rust-house ``` **Registered the old marketplace id?** Run `/plugin marketplace remove orin-dx-agent-plugins` (Claude Code) or `codex plugin marketplace remove orin-dx-agent-plugins` (Codex), then add `orin-dx/wisp-plugins` as above. Upgrading from v4: see [Migrating from v4](#migrating-from-v4). --- ## Quick start Start with `/wisp:work` and describe the change; it picks the mode. Or start a mode directly: | Command | Use it when | Example | What comes back | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `/wisp:work` | Any change, or you are not sure which mode fits | `/wisp:work the export drops rows with empty dates` | The mode it chose, then as below | | `/wisp:explore` | You want to see options before deciding | `/wisp:explore three layouts for the settings page` | Rendered options and a decision log (`option-set@1`) through `muse:sketch` | | `/wisp:spike` | You want to know whether something works here | `/wisp:spike does this queue library run on our Node version?` | A `spike-report@1`: what ran, what was verified, what was not; files only under `.scratch//` | | `/wisp:fix` | Something is broken, or a review left findings | `/wisp:fix login fails when the email has a plus sign` | A test that failed before and passes after, the fix, and other places with the same mistake | | `/wisp:build` | You are building something real | `/wisp:build add CSV import to the contacts API` | The change and its evidence; a spec or plan only where one pays | | `/wisp:check` | You want work verified, or bugs found | `/wisp:check is the retry change done?` | A `verdict@3` from the verifier, or suspected bugs each confirmed or dismissed | | `/wisp:ship` | The work is ready to go out | `/wisp:ship changeset and PR` | Only the courier steps you asked for, confirmed before anything is pushed, posted or published | Every reply opens with the mode, the tier and the brief, and ends with the evidence and what was not checked. An abridged, made-up example: ```text Mode: fix. Tier: shared. Outcome: a login with "a+b@x.com" succeeds. Constraints: the session token format does not change (AGENTS.md). Evidence bar: the repo's test command passes, with a new test that fails on the old code. ...work... Evidence: test command: the new test failed before the fix; all tests pass after. Verifier: pass, round 1. Not verified: the mobile client; SSO logins were not exercised. Next: /wisp:ship ``` When a decision changes scope or cannot be undone, you get a **decision card**: the question, two or three structurally different options, a recommendation, and what happens if you do not answer. Everything else proceeds on a stated `Assumption:`. --- ## The plugin set | Plugin | Use it for | Commands | Agents (tier) | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | [`wisp`](./plugins/wisp/) | Every change: sizes it, states the brief, does the work, verifies where it pays | `work`, `explore`, `spike`, `fix`, `build`, `check`, `ship` | `verifier`, `adversary` (opus/high); `recon` (haiku/low) | | [`courier`](./plugins/courier/) | Commit messages, PRs, changesets, review feedback, release notes | `commit`, `pr`, `changeset`, `receive-feedback`, `post-review`, `release` | `pr-narrator`, `changeset-analyzer` (sonnet/medium); `commit-analyzer` (haiku/low) | | [`muse`](./plugins/muse/) | Seeing rendered options before deciding, and turning the chosen one into work | `sketch`, `promote` | `explorer` (sonnet/medium) | | [`wisp-packs`](./plugins/wisp-packs/) | Making the agent build the way your other repos are built | `load`, `list`, `suggest` | none | | [`mason`](./plugins/mason/) | Building, auditing and evaluating plugins like these | `scaffold-plugin`, `audit-plugin`, `design-schema`, `scaffold-subagent`, `evaluate` | `auditor`, `scaffolder`, `schema-designer` (sonnet/medium); `evaluation-runner` (haiku/low); `evaluation-adjudicator` (opus/high) | In Claude Code a command is `/:`, for example `/courier:pr` or `/wisp-packs:load rust-house`. --- ## How it works ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'flowchart': {'curve': 'basis', 'nodeSpacing': 40, 'rankSpacing': 56}, 'themeVariables': {'fontFamily': 'Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif', 'fontSize': '14px', 'lineColor': '#94a3b8', 'edgeLabelBackground': '#ffffff'}}}%% flowchart LR classDef source fill:#eef2ff,stroke:#6366f1,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#1e1b4b,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; classDef store fill:#f8fafc,stroke:#64748b,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#0f172a,rx:10px,ry:10px; classDef engine fill:#f5f3ff,stroke:#8b5cf6,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#4c1d95,rx:10px,ry:10px; classDef router fill:#fffbeb,stroke:#f59e0b,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#78350f,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; classDef output fill:#ecfdf5,stroke:#10b981,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#064e3b,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; classDef alert fill:#fff1f2,stroke:#f43f5e,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#881337,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; Req["Request

# Wisp Plugins Plugins for Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity that change how a coding agent takes on work, and the agent-side companions to the [Wisp](https://github.com/orin-dx/wisp) project-intelligence library. **The agent works from a brief, review scales with how reversible a change is, and you see decisions and evidence at the edges, not the steps in between.** v5 is one core plugin, `wisp`, plus `courier` (shipping), `muse` (exploration), `wisp-packs` (house rules per repo) and `mason` (plugin authoring). Install `wisp` first; add the others when you need them. - **Brief first:** before any edit the agent states the outcome, the constraints and the evidence bar (the command, test, build or render that proves it). - **Review follows risk:** each change is sized as contained, shared or irreversible. Only shared and irreversible work goes to an independent verifier with a fresh context. - **You see the edges:** a brief and decision cards on the way in; the diff or render, the evidence, a `Not verified:` list and the PR on the way out. --- ## Install **Claude Code** ``` /plugin marketplace add orin-dx/wisp-plugins /plugin install wisp /plugin install courier /plugin install muse /plugin install wisp-packs /plugin install mason ``` **Codex** ```bash codex plugin marketplace add orin-dx/wisp-plugins codex plugin add wisp@wisp-plugins codex plugin add courier@wisp-plugins codex plugin add muse@wisp-plugins codex plugin add wisp-packs@wisp-plugins codex plugin add mason@wisp-plugins ``` `codex plugin list` shows what is available; `codex plugin marketplace upgrade wisp-plugins` refreshes after a release. Codex reads the generated `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`, which points at `dist/codex/`. From a local checkout: `python3 tools/build-codex-marketplace.py`, then `codex plugin marketplace add .`. **Antigravity (AGY)** ```bash agy plugin install https://github.com/orin-dx/wisp-plugins.git ``` AGY uses the same source tree as Claude Code. Whether the v5 hooks and pack injection work there is not verified. The community [`agy-plugins-cli`](https://github.com/ZaunEkko/agy-plugins-cli) (`agy-plugin marketplace add orin-dx/wisp-plugins`, then `agy-plugin add @wisp-plugins`) may not find plugins under `plugins/`; that path is not verified either. **Set it up for a project.** So everyone on a repo gets the plugins in Claude Code, commit this to `.claude/settings.json`: ```json { "extraKnownMarketplaces": { "wisp-plugins": { "source": { "source": "github", "repo": "orin-dx/wisp-plugins" } } }, "enabledPlugins": { "wisp@wisp-plugins": true, "courier@wisp-plugins": true, "wisp-packs@wisp-plugins": true } } ``` and add this to the repo's `AGENTS.md`, which every harness reads (the `Packs:` line is optional; see [Packs](#packs)): ```markdown ## Work Start changes with /wisp:work (or /wisp:fix, /wisp:build, /wisp:check, /wisp:spike, /wisp:explore, /wisp:ship). State the tier, the brief and the evidence bar first; end with the evidence and a "Not verified:" list. Packs: rust-house ``` **Registered the old marketplace id?** Run `/plugin marketplace remove orin-dx-agent-plugins` (Claude Code) or `codex plugin marketplace remove orin-dx-agent-plugins` (Codex), then add `orin-dx/wisp-plugins` as above. Upgrading from v4: see [Migrating from v4](#migrating-from-v4). --- ## Quick start Start with `/wisp:work` and describe the change; it picks the mode. Or start a mode directly: | Command | Use it when | Example | What comes back | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `/wisp:work` | Any change, or you are not sure which mode fits | `/wisp:work the export drops rows with empty dates` | The mode it chose, then as below | | `/wisp:explore` | You want to see options before deciding | `/wisp:explore three layouts for the settings page` | Rendered options and a decision log (`option-set@1`) through `muse:sketch` | | `/wisp:spike` | You want to know whether something works here | `/wisp:spike does this queue library run on our Node version?` | A `spike-report@1`: what ran, what was verified, what was not; files only under `.scratch//` | | `/wisp:fix` | Something is broken, or a review left findings | `/wisp:fix login fails when the email has a plus sign` | A test that failed before and passes after, the fix, and other places with the same mistake | | `/wisp:build` | You are building something real | `/wisp:build add CSV import to the contacts API` | The change and its evidence; a spec or plan only where one pays | | `/wisp:check` | You want work verified, or bugs found | `/wisp:check is the retry change done?` | A `verdict@3` from the verifier, or suspected bugs each confirmed or dismissed | | `/wisp:ship` | The work is ready to go out | `/wisp:ship changeset and PR` | Only the courier steps you asked for, confirmed before anything is pushed, posted or published | Every reply opens with the mode, the tier and the brief, and ends with the evidence and what was not checked. An abridged, made-up example: ```text Mode: fix. Tier: shared. Outcome: a login with "a+b@x.com" succeeds. Constraints: the session token format does not change (AGENTS.md). Evidence bar: the repo's test command passes, with a new test that fails on the old code. ...work... Evidence: test command: the new test failed before the fix; all tests pass after. Verifier: pass, round 1. Not verified: the mobile client; SSO logins were not exercised. Next: /wisp:ship ``` When a decision changes scope or cannot be undone, you get a **decision card**: the question, two or three structurally different options, a recommendation, and what happens if you do not answer. Everything else proceeds on a stated `Assumption:`. --- ## The plugin set | Plugin | Use it for | Commands | Agents (tier) | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | [`wisp`](./plugins/wisp/) | Every change: sizes it, states the brief, does the work, verifies where it pays | `work`, `explore`, `spike`, `fix`, `build`, `check`, `ship` | `verifier`, `adversary` (opus/high); `recon` (haiku/low) | | [`courier`](./plugins/courier/) | Commit messages, PRs, changesets, review feedback, release notes | `commit`, `pr`, `changeset`, `receive-feedback`, `post-review`, `release` | `pr-narrator`, `changeset-analyzer` (sonnet/medium); `commit-analyzer` (haiku/low) | | [`muse`](./plugins/muse/) | Seeing rendered options before deciding, and turning the chosen one into work | `sketch`, `promote` | `explorer` (sonnet/medium) | | [`wisp-packs`](./plugins/wisp-packs/) | Making the agent build the way your other repos are built | `load`, `list`, `suggest` | none | | [`mason`](./plugins/mason/) | Building, auditing and evaluating plugins like these | `scaffold-plugin`, `audit-plugin`, `design-schema`, `scaffold-subagent`, `evaluate` | `auditor`, `scaffolder`, `schema-designer` (sonnet/medium); `evaluation-runner` (haiku/low); `evaluation-adjudicator` (opus/high) | In Claude Code a command is `/:`, for example `/courier:pr` or `/wisp-packs:load rust-house`. --- ## How it works ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'flowchart': {'curve': 'basis', 'nodeSpacing': 40, 'rankSpacing': 56}, 'themeVariables': {'fontFamily': 'Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif', 'fontSize': '14px', 'lineColor': '#94a3b8', 'edgeLabelBackground': '#ffffff'}}}%% flowchart LR classDef source fill:#eef2ff,stroke:#6366f1,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#1e1b4b,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; Install `wisp` first; add the others when you need them. - **Brief first:** before any edit the agent states the outcome, the constraints and the evidence bar (the command, test, build or render that proves it). - **Review follows risk:** each change is sized as contained, shared or irreversible. # wisp — Core **Stage:** Any · **Output:** the change, its evidence and a `Not verified:` list · **Version:** 1.0.0 The one way to start work: `wisp` sizes each change by how hard it is to undo, states what done means and how it will be proven before anything is edited, and spends independent review only where a confident mistake would be costly. --- ## When to use | Situation | Command | | :--- | :--- | | Any change, or you are not sure which path fits | `/wisp:work` | | You want to see options before deciding | `/wisp:explore` | | You want to know whether a tool or approach works here | `/wisp:spike` | | Something is broken, or a review left findings | `/wisp:fix` | | You are building a feature or a change other work will depend on | `/wisp:build` | | You want work verified, or bugs found | `/wisp:check` | | The work is ready to commit, document or release | `/wisp:ship` | Plain requests work too: "fix this bug", "is this done?", "find bugs in this", "does this library work here?", "ship this". --- ## Skills | Skill | What it does | Hands off to | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `wisp/work` | States the brief (outcome, constraints, evidence bar), sizes the tier, picks the mode and review depth; asks you only for decisions that change scope or cannot be undone | `verifier`, `adversary`, `recon`; `muse`, `courier` | | `wisp/explore` | Structurally different options, rendered, with a decision log; # courier — Ship Tooling **Stage:** Ship · **Output:** `release-artifact@3` · **Version:** 5.0.0 Writes what goes out with a change: commit messages, pull request descriptions, changesets and release notes, plus review-feedback triage and posting a drafted review. Six independent skills, not a pipeline. Each reads the diff and any linked spec or requirement, and follows the repository's own conventions where it has them. Courier does not critique code quality; that is the built-in `code-review` skill's job. `/wisp:ship` calls these skills in order (changeset, commit, PR, release) and runs only the ones you ask for. --- ## When to use | Situation | Skill | | :--- | :--- | | You need a commit message that explains why, not only what | `courier/commit` | | You are opening a PR and want a description a reviewer with no context can act on | `courier/pr` | | A user-visible change needs a changeset or changelog entry | `courier/changeset` | | You received review comments on your PR and want the full picture before replying | `courier/receive-feedback` | | You have a drafted review or reply and want it posted to GitHub | `courier/post-review` | | You are cutting a release and need release notes | `courier/release` | Use the skill instead of writing these by hand: each carries rules that freehand text skips. Plain requests work: "commit this", "open a PR", "add a changeset", "address the feedback", "post this review", "cut a release". ## Skills | Skill | What it does | Agent | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `courier/commit` | A conventional commit message from the staged diff, explaining why | `commit-analyzer` | | `courier/pr` | A PR title and body for a reviewer with no context, reporting observed verification and gaps; follows the repo's PR template | `pr-narrator` | | `courier/changeset` | One layered `changeset@3` entry per user-visible outcome, an update to an existing entry, or a recommendation that none is needed | `changeset-analyzer` | | `courier/receive-feedback` | Assembles a review package (diff summary, linked spec, test results, open questions) for feedback on your own PR | none | | `courier/post-review` | Posts an already-drafted review or reply with `gh pr review` or `gh pr comment`, after you confirm | none | | `courier/release` | Aggregates changesets since the last release into a `release-artifact@3`; the version is the highest `semver_impact` | none | ## Agents | Agent | Tier | Does | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `commit-analyzer` | haiku / low | Reads the staged diff and writes a conventional commit message that explains why | | `pr-narrator` | sonnet / medium | Writes the PR title and body from the reviewer's side, assuming no prior context | | `changeset-analyzer` | sonnet / medium | Classifies consumer and semver impact per outcome (`shared/references/delivery/changesets.md`) and writes `changeset@3` entries whose detail scales with that impact | `receive-feedback`, `post-review` and `release` are mechanical, so the skill does the work itself. ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'flowchart': {'curve': 'basis', 'nodeSpacing': 40, 'rankSpacing': 56}, 'themeVariables': {'fontFamily': 'Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif', 'fontSize': '14px', 'lineColor': '#94a3b8', 'edgeLabelBackground': '#ffffff'}}}%% flowchart TD classDef source fill:#eef2ff,stroke:#6366f1,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#1e1b4b,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; classDef engine fill:#f5f3ff,stroke:#8b5cf6,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#4c1d95,rx:10px,ry:10px; classDef router fill:#fffbeb,stroke:#f59e0b,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#78350f,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; classDef output fill:#ecfdf5,stroke:#10b981,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#064e3b,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; Diff["Git diff"] --> Changeset["changeset
changeset-analyzer"] --> CS(["changeset@3"]) CS --> Release["release
aggregates"] --> RelOut(["release-artifact@3"]) Staged["Staged diff"] --> Commit["commit
commit-analyzer"] --> CommitOut(["conventional commit"]) Diff --> PR["pr
pr-narrator"] --> Confirm{{"you confirm"}} --> PROut(["Entire trail opens the PR,
or gh pr create"]) Comments["PR comments"] --> Receive["receive-feedback
assembles"] -->|"review package"| Draft["you or the agent draft a reply"] --> Post["post-review"] --> Reply(["posted reply"]) class Diff,Staged,Comments source class Changeset,PR,Release,Commit,Receive,Draft,Post engine class Confirm router class CS,PROut,RelOut,CommitOut,Reply output ``` ## What it produces - **`changeset@3`** (`shared/schemas/changeset@3.json`). When the repository keeps changesets as files (for example `.changeset/*.md`), each entry is also saved there in the repo's format and bump, through its own tool when it has one. - **`release-artifact@3`** (`shared/schemas/release-artifact@3.json`). Not needed where the repo's release PR aggregates changesets. - **Pull requests:** by default `courier/pr` pushes the branch and creates or links its Entire trail (`entire trail create`); Entire opens the PR from the trail, using the title and body. It runs `gh pr create` only when the repository's instructions say agents open PRs. Opening, pushing and posting always wait for your confirmation. When the work produced `criteria_evidence`, `courier/changeset` takes it as input; otherwise it works from the diff. ## Hooks None. --- ## Install **Claude Code:** `/plugin marketplace add orin-dx/wisp-plugins`, then `/plugin install courier`. **Codex:** `codex plugin marketplace add orin-dx/wisp-plugins`, then `codex plugin add courier@wisp-plugins`. **Antigravity:** see the [root README](../../README.md#install). ## Example After a fix, "add a changeset and open a PR" runs `courier/changeset`, which writes one entry for the user-visible outcome (or says none is needed for an internal change), then `courier/pr`, which shows you the title and body. On your confirmation it pushes the branch and hands them to the branch's Entire trail, which opens the PR. References the agents load at runtime: `shared/references/delivery/commits.md`, `github.md`, `changesets.md`, and `shared/references/authoring/voice.md`.

41:  "round": 1,
60:Follow it exactly, because the file is checked against `option-set@1` and a record in another shape is rejected. Required: `id` (`SKETCH-` and three or more digits), `title`, `brief` (with `problem` and `audience`), `status` (`exploring`, `decided` or `abandoned`), `round` (an integer from 1), `options` (one to five), `fidelity` (always `sketch`) and `reasoning`. Each option needs `id` (`OPT-` and a lowercase slug), `title`, `summary`, `structure` and `status` (`open`, `parked`, `chosen` or `rejected`); every status except `open` needs a `reason`. # muse — Explore and Render **Stage:** Exploration · **Output:** `option-set@1` · **Version:** 5.0.0 Shows you rendered options before anything is decided, then carries the one you choose into real work. Muse is non-binding: no gate, no spec, no tests. It builds structurally different options, renders them and shows them before describing them, keeps a decision log, and stops before implementing. `/wisp:explore` starts `sketch`; specifying and checking a component's props, states and accessibility is `/wisp:build`'s job. --- ## When to use | Situation | Skill | | :--- | :--- | | You want to see a few directions for a screen, component or approach before deciding | `muse/sketch` | | A chosen option, or a spike that worked, should become real work | `muse/promote` | Plain requests work: "show me some options for this screen", "try a few directions", "what could this look like", "promote option B", "that spike worked, make it a feature". ## Skills | Skill | What it does | Agent | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `muse/sketch` | Builds and renders three structurally different options per round (different arrangement, interaction model or hierarchy, not different colors), shows the renders first, and keeps a decision log in an `option-set@1` | `explorer` | | `muse/promote` | Turns a chosen option or a working spike into a `requirement@1` carrying the decision, the approved render, and what was and was not verified; the only route from exploration into real work | none | ## Agents | Agent | Tier | Does | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `explorer` | sonnet / medium | Builds and renders one option for a sketch, writing only to a scratch directory, and returns an `option-set@1` holding only that option. Never ranks options. Started by `sketch`. | ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'flowchart': {'curve': 'basis', 'nodeSpacing': 40, 'rankSpacing': 56}, 'themeVariables': {'fontFamily': 'Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif', 'fontSize': '14px', 'lineColor': '#94a3b8', 'edgeLabelBackground': '#ffffff'}}}%% flowchart LR classDef source fill:#eef2ff,stroke:#6366f1,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#1e1b4b,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; classDef engine fill:#f5f3ff,stroke:#8b5cf6,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#4c1d95,rx:10px,ry:10px; classDef output fill:#ecfdf5,stroke:#10b981,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#064e3b,rx:10px,ry:10px,font-weight:600; Intent["Design intent
free text or requirement@1"] --> Sketch["sketch
explorer builds and renders"] Sketch --> Options(["option-set@1"]) Options -.->|"another round"| Sketch Options -->|"you choose"| Promote["promote"] Spike(["spike-report@1"]) --> Promote Promote --> Req(["requirement@1"]) Req --> Build["wisp
/wisp:build"] class Intent source class Sketch,Promote,Build engine class Options,Req,Spike output ``` You decide; nothing here ranks or advises. After about five rounds without a decision, `sketch` offers to narrow the brief, park the exploration or abandon it. ## What it produces - **Renders and a board:** each option as a static page under `.scratch///`, rendered at the brief's viewports and themes (default 390x844 and 1440x900), with `.scratch//board.html` showing them side by side. If nothing can render, it says so and gives the command that opens the files. - **`option-set@1`** (`shared/schemas/option-set@1.json`), written to `docs/sketches/.json`: the anchor brief, a status (`exploring`, `decided`, `abandoned`), one to five options each with its own status and reason, assumptions, open questions, renders, and an append-only decision log. - **`requirement@1`** (`shared/schemas/requirement@1.json`) from `promote`, written where the repository keeps requirements (a file or its issue tracker), linking the sketch or spike. `sketch` writes only under `.scratch//` and to `docs/sketches/.json`, and never edits existing source, configuration or specs. Add `.scratch/` to your ignore file. ## Hooks None. --- ## Install **Claude Code:** `/plugin marketplace add orin-dx/wisp-plugins`, then `/plugin install muse`. **Codex:** `codex plugin marketplace add orin-dx/wisp-plugins`, then `codex plugin add muse@wisp-plugins`. **Antigravity:** see the [root README](../../README.md#install). ## Example `/muse:sketch three layouts for the billing settings page, using our tokens` writes a brief, builds three options (say a single long form, tabs by topic, and a summary with edit drawers), renders each at phone and desktop width, and shows the board before describing anything. You answer "B, but with the summary from C"; the decision goes in the log and the next round stays inside that direction. When you are happy, `/muse:promote` turns the chosen option into a `requirement@1` for `/wisp:build`.

lines: - **What a pack may do:** it never adds a command the repo does not declare; the repo's `AGENTS.md` and your instructions win over it; it may tighten a check, but loosening one needs the owner.

- **Write one:** add `plugins/wisp-packs/packs/<name>.md` (lowercase letters, digits and hyphens). The first line says when it applies. Each rule states the outcome and ends with what enforces it: `[lint]`, `[type]` or `[review]`. End with a file to imitate. A rule goes in a shared pack only when it holds in at least two repos. Run `just marketplace-sync` so the Codex bundle carries it.
